sections.heading: Galaxy Launches Bitcoin Quantum Readiness Initiative to Protect Bitcoin's Cryptographic Foundations
paragraphs: Commits up to $5 million in developer grants; establishes Quantum Advisory Council; calls on industry to join the effort

Galaxy today announced the launch of the Galaxy Bitcoin Quantum Readiness Initiative, a multi-pillar program dedicated to preparing Bitcoin for the threat posed by advances in quantum computing. The initiative includes up to $5 million in grant funding for developers working on post-quantum solutions for Bitcoin, a dedicated research and publishing program through Galaxy Research, and the formation of a Quantum Advisory Council of leading experts in quantum computing and post-quantum cryptography.

Bitcoin's security relies on elliptic curve cryptography, which could be broken by a sufficiently powerful quantum computer. While no cryptographically relevant quantum computer exists today, the expected timeline for one to be built is compressing. The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) finalized its first post-quantum cryptography standards in 2024, and a recent executive order set a 2031 deadline for the federal government to defend against quantum attacks on classical cryptography.

“As leaders in the digital assets space, we believe it’s important that we help be part of the solution to any potential threat quantum computing poses to Bitcoin,” said Mike Novogratz, Founder and CEO of Galaxy. “This initiative reflects that commitment, creating practical steps to research, fund and support the work that keeps Bitcoin secure for the long run.”

Bitcoin’s decentralized governance means protocol upgrades, including those designed to protect against a quantum threat, can take years to design, review, test and deploy. To date, the developers working on quantum resilience for Bitcoin remain few relative to the scale of the challenge.
To address these gaps, the initiative is structured around three pillars:

Developer Grant Program: Galaxy is committing up to $5 million in grant funding for developers and researchers working on post-quantum cryptographic solutions for Bitcoin. Priority areas include implementation and review of quantum-resistant transaction proposals, development and integration of post-quantum signature schemes into Bitcoin, tooling for wallet and custodian migration, and formal security audits of proposed implementations. Grants will be evaluated individually and disbursed on a milestone basis and Galaxy expects to begin accepting applications immediately. Those interested in applying for grants can email [email protected].

Research and Publishing Program: Galaxy Research will publish ongoing analysis of the quantum threat to Bitcoin and the evolving landscape of developer efforts to address it with the aim of providing rigorous and accessible information on this topic for institutional investors, policymakers, and the developer community.

Quantum Advisory Council: A Quantum Advisory Council has been formed to guide the initiative's research, evaluate grant proposals, and ensure Galaxy's efforts are grounded in the best available expertise. Meeting regularly with Galaxy's research team and executives, the Council will advise Galaxy on quantum-related preparedness and contribute to the initiative's public-facing research output. The inaugural members of the Council are:
Barry Sanders, Professor and Scientific Director of Quantum City at University of Calgary
Eran Tromer, Professor of Computer Science at Boston University

“There's a gap between the quantum computing world, which is moving fast, and the Bitcoin development world, which is just beginning to engage with post-quantum cryptography in earnest,” said Alex Thorn, Head of Firmwide Research at Galaxy. “Galaxy's role is to bridge that gap through research that makes the threat legible to investors and policymakers, as well as grants that fund the developers doing the hardest technical work.”

“Quantum timelines continue to compress, and governments and industries worldwide are moving to prepare for potential implications. Bitcoin should be no exception,” said Barry Sanders, Professor and Scientific Director of Quantum City at University of Calgary. “I’m proud to advise Galaxy as it takes a leadership role in that effort.”

Galaxy understands that others in the industry may also be pledging funds toward preparing Bitcoin for quantum computing, and wholeheartedly supports those efforts. The firm welcomes institutions and Bitcoin stakeholders interested in co-funding grants or contributing research, and developers working on post-quantum solutions for Bitcoin.
For more information about the initiative, grant applications, and other inquiries, contact [email protected].

paragraphs: These applications turn usage into transactions by solving real user problems and delivering outcomes users are willing to pay for, with repeat usage built in.

sections.heading: Startups: Apply today for up to $100,000 in Grafana Cloud credits
paragraphs: At Grafana Labs, we believe in providing observability solutions for organizations of every size and stage. That’s why we have free tiers and enterprise plans and everything in between. But across our broad spectrum of users, startups have particular needs and challenges.

For example, if they catch fire, they are going to need to scale rapidly. It’s a good problem to have, but it also carries financial risk. Founders typically have limited funds, and they’re often caught between reinvesting in that growth and simply keeping the lights on. But it doesn’t have to be like that.

To alleviate this pressure and avoid some of those tradeoffs, we are excited to introduce the [Grafana Labs Startup Program](https://grafana-labs.typeform.com/to/cSI7ohks/?pg=blog&plcmt=body-txt). Announced today as part of [ObservabilityCON 2024](https://grafana.com/blog/2024/09/24/observabilitycon-2024-announcements/?pg=blog&plcmt=body-txt), the program includes up to $100,000 in [Grafana Cloud](https://grafana.com/products/cloud/?pg=blog&plcmt=body-txt) credits to eligible startups for 12 months or until their next round of funding.

Telemetry management platform [Datable.io](https://www.datable.io/) is among the first to be accepted into the program. CEO Julian Giuca says Grafana Cloud provides the startup with an observability solution to monitor customer instances in its single-tenant architecture. The credits, he added, are helping them dedicate more of their energy toward growing the business.

“Grafana Cloud’s solutions and open source approach gives us a ton of flexibility, and the startup program has allowed us to focus on execution without worrying about our monitoring stack,” Julian says. “We strongly believe in OpenTelemetry, which made Grafana Cloud an easy choice. Come by our office any time of day, and you’ll see a Grafana dashboard up on multiple screens. It’s a critical part of our daily operations, and it gives us the confidence our systems are healthy and customers happy.”

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Again and again, we see startups come to us after getting burned by observability solutions that seemed like the right fit but ultimately became cost prohibitive as they scaled. Moreover, these same startups find themselves locked into proprietary platforms that don’t allow them to leverage open standards or adapt their platform to evolving practices, making it difficult to avail themselves of the benefits of an open and composable platform like Grafana Cloud.

With the Grafana Labs Startup Program, our goal is to help startups head off this problem before sticker shock ever happens. We want to be good partners to the startup community, helping them grow their business long-term so they’re able to create amazing products without the stress of an unexpectedly high observability bill.

And if, for whatever reason, you eventually want to transition away from Grafana Cloud — I know, hard to believe —rest assured that we embrace openness and composability so you don’t have to worry about lock-in at all.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: All new customers (including those with Grafana Cloud Free accounts) are eligible to apply to the program, as well as those already using Grafana OSS who want to move to a fully managed solution. Grafana Labs will determine which applicants will be offered admission into the startup program at its sole discretion.

In terms of requirements for participating should you be accepted to the program, we ask that you agree to be a reference customer. We may also ask you to mutually agree to marketing activities, such as guest blogs and speaking at events. Ideally, applicants will have raised less than $10 million in funding and be under 25 employees, but please apply even if you do not meet these guidelines.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: On December 2, 2024, G DAO approved Proposal GP35, securing a $5 million budget to fund strategic initiatives within the Gravity ecosystem.

The Gravity Developer Grant Program is a funding initiative designed to support developers and innovators in building applications within the Gravity ecosystem. By empowering builders, Gravity aims to enable the development of tools like decentralized applications, developer infrastructure, and community-driven projects that address user needs, encourage collaboration, and contribute to the ecosystem’s continuous growth.

paragraphs: Gravity invites developers and teams to join our ecosystem, utilizing our high-performance infrastructure to build scalable dApps that can drive real-world adoption. To be eligible for the Developer Grant Program, projects must meet one or more of the following criteria:
Built for Gravity: Projects should either run exclusively on the Gravity Chain or designate Gravity as a primary network in their architecture.
Mainnet Availability: Projects must have a fully functional Mainnet version that is live and accessible to users.

Clear Development Roadmap: For projects that are not yet live, a detailed go-to-market (GTM) plan is required. The plan should include development timelines, strategies for acquiring users, and clear launch goals.

name: Interledger Foundation: Digital Financial Services Grant
description: $350K per recipient for regulated financial service providers (credit unions, co-ops, remittance companies, wallets) launching live payment services on the open Interledger network, with 18 months of support. It focuses on Latin America (Colombia) but is open worldwide. Shortlisted applicants submit a full proposal in early 2027.

sections.heading: Digital Financial Services
paragraphs: Supporting financial service providers to build and participate in open, interoperable payment networks.
The Digital Financial Services Grant supports financial service providers that are ready to implement interoperable payment infrastructure using Rhyza and Interledger technologies.

Across markets, digital payments often operate within disconnected systems, creating friction for financial institutions and limiting how easily consumers and businesses can transact across providers, networks and borders.

Through this grant, the Interledger Foundation will support organizations to implement and pilot open payment infrastructure. Each funded institution can connect with others, and every connection helps build a more open, interoperable financial system.
Selected institutions may receive grants of up to USD $350,000 to implement and complete projects within 18 months.

sections.heading: Who it is for
paragraphs: The grant is designed for regulated financial service providers, or organizations with a credible pathway toward the regulatory authorization required for their proposed services.

sections.heading: What it supports
bullets: Integration of Rhyza, the open source software that connects your existing infrastructure to Interledger and Open Payments.
Technical development, infrastructure and testing for cross-border interoperable payments

sections.heading: How it works
bullets: Number of awards: Up to three grants will be awarded. We will prioritize proposals with a focus on projects in Colombia and the broader Americas, although global applications are welcome.
Phase 1 Application deadline: Friday, December 11, 2026 at 11:59 pm ET 2026 @ 11:59 pm ET.
Phase 2 is anticipated to run from February 1 to 26, 2027, and will be open to selected applications from Phase 1.

sections.heading: What We Are Looking to Build
paragraphs: We want to support institutions that can demonstrate how our open, interoperable payment infrastructure can work in practice: connecting systems, establishing network relationships, testing transactions, serving customers, and generating lessons that can support future implementations. By bringing more financial service providers into interoperable networks, the projects we fund can help advance the Interledger Foundation’s mission to foster an inclusive global financial system.

Our interoperable payments infrastructure includes Rhyza - a free, open source software that connects a financial service provider’s existing infrastructure to Interledger, so it can make payments across systems and currencies and offer Open Payments-enabled accounts and services. Open Payments is an API standard that enables secure, consent-based payment initiation and management. Together, these technologies support accessible, interoperable payment services.

sections.heading: How to Apply
paragraphs: Applications for Phase 1 are open until Friday, December 11, 2026 at 11:59 pm ET.

For Phase 1, we ask all interested organizations to submit a short application form (opens in a new tab), providing key details about your proposal. Applicants with a strong Phase 1 submission will be invited to Phase 2, where a more detailed proposal shall be requested. Phase 2 is anticipated to run from February 1 to 26, 2027.
Please review the 2027 Digital Financial Services Grant, EOI Resource Kit (opens in a new tab)and our full FAQ for program guidance and resources to help you develop your proposals for Phase 1.

sections.heading: People’s Clearinghouse
paragraphs: People’s Clearinghouse (PCH) is a digital payments platform that seeks to connect Mexico’s community banks and savings cooperatives with the national financial system and international remittance networks. Led by AMUCSS and built on open-source Interledger technology, the project is working to route remittances straight into community bank accounts instead of cash, so money stays local as savings and credit.

With support from the Interledger Foundation, PCH has grown into a production-ready platform, demonstrated live at the 2025 Interledger Summit in Mexico City. It expects Central Bank authorization and launch by the end of 2026, reaching several hundred thousand people across its partner network, many gaining access to digital payments for the first time.
Watch our mini-documentary about PCH and their work.

sections.heading: Our Grantees
paragraphs: To learn more about the work and projects of past recipients of the Digital Financial Services Grant, check out our Grantee Directory.
We are looking for financial services providers that are ready to move beyond exploration and into implementation when it comes to interoperability.
Applicants should have a clear use case for interoperability and a realistic pathway toward implementing and testing their proposed solution.

The Interledger Foundation is particularly interested in projects that strengthen participation in Colombia, the wider Americas, and across multiple markets or regions where integration can create broader interoperability and network value.
Selected projects may receive $350,000 USD for an 18-month implementation period.

Throughout the 18-month implementation period, grantees will not only have funding ($350,000 USD) but also support from the Interledger Foundation's program and technical teams, including regular implementation reviews focused on progress, technical integration, challenges, and next steps.

The program is designed not only to support individual implementations, but also to generate practical knowledge about what is required to deploy interoperable payment infrastructure across different markets and operating environments.
Grant funds may support activities across five key areas, including, but not limited to, the following:
bullets: Regulatory authorization or a credible pathway toward authorization;
Technical and operational readiness to undertake an integration;
The ability to pilot services with customers, merchants, or strategic partners.
Regular engagement with Interledger program and technical leads;
Opportunities to share implementation learnings and project outcomes;
Access to relevant technical resources and documentation; and
Opportunities to contribute knowledge and practical insights to the development of open payment infrastructure.
Regulatory readiness – Appropriate authorization, or a credible pathway to obtaining it.
Technical capacity – Infrastructure, technical expertise, or implementation partners capable of supporting a Rhyza integration.
Operational and compliance readiness – Strong governance, staffing, risk management, customer due diligence, security, and data protection processes.
Clear market need – A defined use case and an existing or prospective customer base.
Pilot readiness – Ability to move beyond a prototype and test with real users, customers, merchants, or partners.
Sustainability – A viable plan to maintain and grow the service beyond the grant period.
Technical integration – RhyzaRafiki integration with Open Payments implementation, API development, infrastructure upgrades, security, and testing.
Compliance and regulatory readiness – Legal and regulatory assessments, licensing support, risk management, data protection, and compliance improvements.
Network participation – Peering arrangements, settlement and operational testing, transaction monitoring, and reporting.
Pilot deployment – Customer onboarding, partner or merchant engagement, pilot operations, real-world transaction testing, and evaluation.
Knowledge sharing – Technical documentation, open source contributions, implementation guides, peer learning, and case studies.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: The Financial Services Provider Grant application process, first phase, the Expression of Interest (EOI) opens on Monday, November 2, 2026, and closes on Friday, December 11, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET.

The EOI is the first phase of the application process and is intended for financial institutions and financial service providers that are positioned to integrate interoperable payment infrastructure and pilot a real-world digital financial service. At this phase, we want to understand your organization, the financial service or payment challenge you are seeking to address, the relevance of interoperable payment infrastructure to your proposed work, and your organization’s readiness to undertake a meaningful integration and pilot.

Applicants are not expected to submit a fully developed technical architecture or detailed implementation plan at the EOI stage. The purpose of this initial application is to help the Interledger Foundation identify organizations and concepts with strong potential to advance to Phase 2: Full Proposal.

Before submitting, we strongly encourage applicants to review the Program Resource Kit, which provides detailed guidance on the application process, program objectives, and expectations, along with additional information and resources to help applicants prepare and submit their applications.

Submission of an EOI does not guarantee advancement to Phase 2. Selected applicants will be invited to submit a Full Proposal with additional technical, implementation, regulatory, budget, and organizational details.
If you have questions or need clarification as you prepare your submission, please contact us at financialservices@interledger.org.

The Interledger-NextGen Higher Education program supports universities in building the next generation of leaders, innovators, and advocates for inclusive, open, and interoperable digital finance. Through partnerships with higher education institutions, the Interledger Foundation (ILF) creates opportunities for undergraduate and graduate students to explore real-world financial inclusion challenges, engage with open-payment technologies such as the Interledger Protocol, and design more equitable payment systems.

The program aligns with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and ILF’s broader commitment to expanding digital financial access for underrepresented groups and vulnerable populations. Through NextGen, ILF invests in diverse talent pipelines and supports universities in creating educational, technical, and community-based pathways that prepare students to contribute to a more inclusive digital economy.

This application is the first stage of the Interledger–NextGen Higher Education Grant application process. At this stage, institutions are not required to submit a full project proposal. Applicants should submit a concise Letter of Intent (template available) that introduces the institution and proposed project at a high level, including the intended participants, proposed activities, anticipated outcomes, and overall alignment with the objectives of the NextGen Higher Education Grant. The LOI must be submitted on the institution’s official letterhead and signed by an authorized university representative. Shortlisted applicants will be invited to proceed to Phase 2 and submit a more detailed full proposal.
Before starting your application, please review the Program Application Resource Kit carefully for information on eligibility, selection criteria, program expectations, and application guidance.
If you have any questions, please feel free to contact us at nextgen@interledger.org.
Applications close on Monday, December 14, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT. We encourage you to submit ahead of the deadline to avoid last-minute issues.

name: Livepeer Grants
description: Livepeer Grants provides funding to projects, ideas and events that benefit the Livepeer ecosystem.

sections.heading: This repository is deprecated
paragraphs: This repository is no longer maintained. To apply for a grant, visit the Livepeer Grants homepage.

sections.heading: Requirements
bullets: We are open to funding projects built by teams or individuals, although it helps to have both product/UX + backend for the apps. Find people with complimentary skill sets to join you and collaborate by joining Discord and posting in the #web3-app-ideas channel.
Grants must be achievable within a 3 month timeline

Projects must display a "Powered by Livepeer" watermark, when applicable, to their application. It must be visible while a viewer is watching the video, whether that's in the player itself or in another location that would be easily seen by a viewer.

sections.heading: Grant Types
paragraphs: There are 3 types of grants to support supply and demand for Livepeer’s open video infrastructure. Please choose the one most appropriate for you.

sections.heading: Microgrants - up to $2,000 USD
paragraphs: Microgrants are geared towards tightly scoped projects with a clear deliverable that can be completed in 1 month or less. Examples of such projects may be:
bullets: Hackathon participants who want to complete a feature using Livepeer
Existing projects looking to polish their Livepeer integrations with a well-defined sprint
Educational guides/tutorials/videos targeted at a specific audience teaching them how to build with Livepeer.

sections.heading: Video Disruptor grants - up to $15,000 USD
paragraphs: The Video Disruptor grant is intended for dedicated teams looking to conduct cutting-edge video research and/or explore novel, user-centered web3 applications that leverage Livepeer’s decentralized video compute network. We are interested in teams looking to apply tools like Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, AR/VR, etc to video in a web3 context. We also are interested in teams utilizing other web3 protocols and concepts like FVMs, zK-proofs, etc to create entirely new video experiences and tooling.

We will also consider projects that either disrupt or offer entirely new video experiences vs incumbent, web2 applications. However, teams must demonstrate the ability to engage the community (ideally the team or project already has a large existing community) in a meaningful way to foster fast adoption, growth, and feedback.
Projects must be completed within 3 months or less with clearly defined monthly milestones.

sections.heading: Open Livepeer Network grants
paragraphs: Open grants will be awarded to individuals and teams building tooling and applications to support supply-side node operations, delegation and overall health of the Livepeer Network. Examples of past open network grants include bots for better governance, educational content on how to get started as an Orchestrator or Delegator, tools to better parse/debug logs, etc.
Apply for an Open Livepeer Network Grant here

sections.heading: How to apply
bullets: Submit an issue. Product-based proposals must include specs in the submission. Include mockups, technical milestones, and time estimates. When in doubt breakdown milestones further.

Application will be reviewed by Livepeer Grants, which meets bi-weekly to discuss all on-going and proposed grants. (If you are interested in joining Livepeer Grants, ping @hansy, @shann, @adam, or @ericxtang in the #community-grants Discord channel.) Applications will receive a decision for funding within 2-4 weeks of applying.

Approved grants will receive 20% of the total grant value upfront, followed by graduated payments in the form of milestone completions. Payment is made in LPT (on Arbitrum) based on the USD value of the milestone. The price of LPT used to make the payments is determined using a rolling 30-day average from the time the transaction is queued.

sections.heading: Grants Application Guideline
paragraphs: Note: This repo is migrated from the previous repo to kick start the new grants process
bullets: Measurable result: There should be success metrics for the grant proposal. The success metrics measure the impact on the community.
Achievable: The proposal should be feasible - and sufficient research should be done ahead of time for its feasibility. If it’s a research grant, a well-formed problem statement should be included.

Demonstration of capability: The grant proposal party should demonstrate sufficient experience to successfully achieve the end goal outlined in the proposal. Prior experience in a similar area is highly preferred.
Impact for Livepeer: The grant proposal should have a direct impact on the success of Livepeer and its community. The grant should be impactful to the success of the proposal.

name: Merge Grants
description: Merge Grant is a micro-grant initiative designed to give ambitious builders resources as they pursue compelling projects. You get $50-$1,000 plus support, with zero equity or future obligations.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: No equity · No repayment · No board seat

sections.heading: Mission
paragraphs: Solo Grant is a microgrant program for solo builders. We cut a belief check — $100 to $1,000 — for the parts, compute, and materials that turn a passion project into the first version that works. It's a vote of confidence with a dollar amount attached, not an investment: no equity, no repayment, no board seat.

sections.heading: What it funds
paragraphs: Not salaries, runway, pitch decks, a nicer logo, conference travel, or "market research." Parts, not payroll.

sections.heading: Written application
paragraphs: Keep it real. The strongest applications read like a text to a friend — plain words, real detail, obvious energy. Cover:

sections.heading: Personal background
bullets: ·Your story and what pulls you toward this project

sections.heading: Project description
bullets: ·What you're making and why it's uniquely compelling

sections.heading: Budget breakdown
paragraphs: Itemize it like a bill of materials. Every line should be a real part with a real price:
Be specific. Lean, researched budgets get funded — we size the check to the build, not the dream.

sections.heading: Application Process
bullets: 01Submit the form — about five minutes, no deck, no warm intro.
02Review — we read everything and reply by email.
03Interview — 15 relaxed minutes, builder to builder.
04Decision — on average, about ten days from application to funded; money wired the same week we say yes.

name: Mina Protocol Grants
description: Anyone can participate in zkIgnite. Whether you’re a developer, founder, designer, marketer, or just someone interested in building infra for zkApp developers, there’s a place for you in the program.

sections.heading: Who can participate in zkIgnite?
paragraphs: Anyone can participate in zkIgnite. Whether you’re a developer, founder, designer, marketer, or just someone interested in building infra for zkApp developers, there’s a place for you in the program.

sections.heading: What are the two different 'tracks'?
paragraphs: Track is another word for ‘path’ or ‘journey’ within zkIgnite.The **zkApp track**is for zero-knowledge applications, written using SnarkyJS and deployed on Mina Protocol. User personas will vary, and won’t just be developer-focused. The D**ev Tooling track** is aimed at funding ‘start-ups for start-ups’. The end users of these applications or services will be developers who are building zkApps and need these primitives to build successfully.If you have any questions about which track your proposal belongs to, please ask the Mina Foundation (MF) community team. Please note the MF community team reserves the right to move proposals to the correct track, and will contact you to discuss if that’s the case for your proposal.

sections.heading: How do I come up with a proposal idea for zkApp or Dev Tooling track?
paragraphs: The gatherings during Weeks 1 – 4 will be focused on ideation and proposal writing. We’ll do group ideation sessions, panels, and ‘AMA’ sessions where you’ll have the chance to brainstorm ideas and get immediate feedback from builders and experts.

sections.heading: How many people can be part of a proposal team?
paragraphs: There is no limit to the number of team members.

sections.heading: How much funding can I receive for my proposal?
paragraphs: Builders will be proposing their own funding tiers and milestones. The recommended funding range is varied depending on the scope of the proposal, but the proposed work should cover **a period of 3 months.**

sections.heading: I already have a zkApp business, can I still participate in zkIgnite?
paragraphs: Yes. If you have an existing zkApp business, you can participate as long as your proposal details exactly how the funding will be used, and what milestones you plan to hit over a 3-month time period.

sections.heading: I got funded as part of Cohort 1, can I submit a proposal for Cohort 2 or future cohorts?
paragraphs: Yes, however you will be required to share what progress you have made on your project, and your proposed milestones for Cohort 2 must be a progression from the proposed milestones for Cohort 1. Cohort 1 milestones will be presented on August 2nd, and the final proposal revisions are due on August 16th. If you are submitting for follow-on funding, electors will review your Cohort 1 milestones before allocating further funding. If you are submitting a proposal for a new project, your previously funded project will still be reviewed.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Yes! You will be required to submit a new proposal and go through the process again, but it’s recommended that you link out to your previous cohort’s proposal so previous comments and feedback can be referenced.

sections.heading: Who decides on which proposals to fund?
paragraphs: A team of electors allocates funding for each track.

sections.heading: What kind of support will I receive after my proposal is selected for funding?
paragraphs: For each cohort, after the funding stage, there will be workshops that cover setting up a business, refining a go-to-market strategy, and more. In addition to the gatherings, you’ll be paired with a mentor who will work with you to provide technical guidance, give feedback, and help you prepare for the final ‘milestones’ presentation. Funded projects will be required to present their work at the 3 month mark to a panel of investors in order to receive the final tranche of funding + MINA bonus. There will also be opportunities to connect with potential investors as part of the final pitch.

name: Mozilla Foundation Awards & Fellowships
description: Funding technologists, researchers, and open-source advocates creating trustworthy AI, decentralized web infrastructure, and public-interest technology.

sections.heading: Funding a better tech future
paragraphs: Mozilla Foundation funds changemakers who refuse to accept the status quo in tech, and they’re building better.

sections.heading: The future is still ours to build.
paragraphs: Right now, a handful of companies are building the technology the rest of us live with, from the apps on our phones to the AI showing up in clinics, classrooms, and city halls. Their choices decide who benefits, whose languages get spoken, and what it all costs our planet and our privacy. And those choices are quickly becoming the infrastructure we’ll all be living inside for decades.
But none of this is locked in yet. Investing in alternatives now, while these technologies are still taking shape, can keep a few companies’ choices from becoming everyone’s defaults.

Mozilla Foundation funds the changemakers who believe there’s a better way, and then go build it. They’re educators teaching students how to create technology differently, builders making tools sized for the communities they serve, and artists showing us what technology can be when it’s made to serve people.

sections.heading: We know what it takes for better alternatives to thrive.
paragraphs: Almost thirty years ago, Mozilla took on a one-size-fits-all browser with open-source code and a community of people who believed the web should belong to everyone. That fight taught us what it takes for an alternative to last: patient funding, hands-on support, and a community that shows up when things get hard. Our grantmaking is designed to provide all three because we know that’s what better tech needs to thrive.
Over the last decade, Mozilla Foundation has invested more than $35 million in people and projects building a better technology future.

We make these investments because the technology that serves people best is built differently. It’s built closer to the people it affects, it’s accountable to the communities it serves, and it’s open enough that others can build on it. That kind of work rarely gets early backing from markets that reward speed and scale, so we step in early and stay through the stretch where most promising ideas run out of runway.

sections.heading: Find where you work fits
paragraphs: There is no single path to a better technology future. It takes leaders who can move the field, educators changing how technology is taught, partners who can move resources where they matter, and builders creating alternatives for their communities. Explore our funding programs to see where your work might fit.

sections.heading: Artists Make Tech (AMT)
paragraphs: Funding artists building tech’s future from the start.

sections.heading: We fund, you build.
paragraphs: But you never have to do it alone. A grant from Mozilla Foundation comes with people attached. You’ll get coaching from folks who’ve built products, organizations, and movements, and you’ll meet peers across the world who are wrestling with the same problems you are. At gatherings like MozFest, you’ll swap ideas with builders, educators, and artists from across the globe and leave with new partners and possibilities. The funding helps you get started, but it’s the community that keeps you building long after the grant ends.

Working in tandem with various partners, the EcoBoost program provides full lifecycle support for high-potential projects.
First announced at Consesus 2019, EcoBoost is a US $100 million initiative designed to grow the Neo ecosystem.
Operated by the Neo Global Development EcoGrowth department, the program works by building up a partner network to provide assistance to Neo-based projects.

EcoBoost partners are leveraged to provide full lifecycle support to Neo projects, based on the individual requirements of each project. For example, media partners can assist with outreach and publicity, exchange partners can help list tokens and stimulate liquidity, and institutional partners can provide industry resources.
EcoBoost partners will benefit from business growth opportunities provided by access to the Neo ecosystem and its global community.
The Neo Global Development EcoGrowth team will work with EcoBoost partners and projects to ensure mutually beneficial outcomes for all participants.

Neo EcoFund is an investment fund established by the Neo Foundation. Its goal is to bring diversified help to the Neo ecosystem while creating long-term value and sustainable returns for Neo Foundation.
Neo EcoFund was established in 2018 and has continued to contribute to the expansion and incubation of Neo ecosystem.
The Neo General Grants Program is primarily focused on funding the development of tools and infrastructure for the Neo Blockchain.

The Neo Foundation supports teams that are capable of executing outstanding blockchain software development initiatives that improve the Neo ecosystem.Examples include developer tools such as SDKs, nodes, layer2 protocols, IDE plugins, and infrastructure protocols. We expect teams and deliverables to be adoption driven, developer friendly, and delivered on-time.

The average funding for a project is between $5,000 to $50,000, with the typical maximum funding around $100,000. However, if a project can provide extraordinary value to the Neo ecosystem, additional funding may be possible. Generally, the Neo Foundation decides the funding for a project based on the time, difficulty, importance or priority to the Neo ecosystem and the developer-friendly nature of the project. Most of the projects should be expected to be completed within 6 months.

Grants may be applied for in stages for new projects with complexity, or for existing projects with major new capabilities or upgrades. For existing projects, teams need to complete and deliver on the previous grant as described in their application before receiving additional funds. The Neo Foundation Grants Committee will decide whether to approve the new grant application.
Neo is currently looking for talented developers to take on the following projects.

Neo is an open source, community driven platform for decentralized applications. From its beginning, Neo has been developed through GitHub open source contributions. Anyone can make contributions to the Neo core code base, including shipping new features, proposing NEPs, submitting patches, improving documentation, etc.
Developers who have made outstanding contributions to the Neo core codebase, after being evaluated by the Neo Foundation, will be offered the opportunity to become Core Developers.

Core Developers are empowered to manage and evolve the Neo core codebase and are deeply involved in Neo's technical and engineering decisions; therefore they are required to participate actively and regularly.

Note that community contributors who become ‘Core Developers’ are not employees of the Neo Foundation (NF) or Neo Global Development (NGD). Core Developers can choose their preferred way of contributing to the Neo protocol. However, we expect that you always do so with good intentions and never with the intention of harm.
Core Developers will gain the following permissions and honors; at the same time, they need to assume corresponding responsibilities:

As a Core Developer, in addition to the opportunity to work on the most cutting-edge technology in the blockchain industry and grow your personal brand, the Neo Foundation also provides financial rewards for contributions to Neo. Generally, the Core Developer Grants adopts a two-part reward model.
Note that all the grants will be paid in equivalent NEO.
To encourage substantial improvements to the Neo protocol layer, the Neo Foundation will evaluate the contributions of PRs merged into the master branch, including:

Working in tandem with various partners, the EcoBoost program provides full lifecycle support for high-potential projects.
First announced at Consesus 2019, EcoBoost is a US $100 million initiative designed to grow the Neo ecosystem.
Operated by the Neo Global Development EcoGrowth department, the program works by building up a partner network to provide assistance to Neo-based projects.

EcoBoost partners are leveraged to provide full lifecycle support to Neo projects, based on the individual requirements of each project. For example, media partners can assist with outreach and publicity, exchange partners can help list tokens and stimulate liquidity, and institutional partners can provide industry resources.
EcoBoost partners will benefit from business growth opportunities provided by access to the Neo ecosystem and its global community.
The Neo Global Development EcoGrowth team will work with EcoBoost partners and projects to ensure mutually beneficial outcomes for all participants.

name: Neon Open Source Program
description: Neon’s Open Source Program provides monthly cash sponsorships (from a $200k+ annual pool) via GitHub Sponsors for 6-month renewable terms, plus optional Neon and AI Gateway credits (up to $5k each). Open to any active public open-source project. Requires only a sponsorship logo placement.

sections.heading: Apply for the Open Source Program
paragraphs: Get sponsorship for the open source you maintain

Developers build on open source that a small number of maintainers keep running. Neon commits a minimum of $200,000 a year to sponsoring those maintainers in cash. Each sponsored project receives a monthly amount from that pool through GitHub Sponsors. In return, your project shows the Neon logo, labeled as a sponsorship, in one place you choose.
Your project doesn't need to use Neon or Postgres to apply.

sections.heading: What you get
bullets: Monthly cash sponsorshipNeon sponsors your project through GitHub Sponsors with a fixed monthly amount for a six-month term, paid from its annual sponsorship pool. You set up payouts and tax details in your GitHub Sponsors profile.
Renewable termsNear the end of each six-month term, we review the sponsorship with you and decide whether to renew it. Sponsorships don't renew automatically.

Neon and AI Gateway creditsProjects we support can also receive up to $5,000 in Neon credits and up to $5,000 in Neon AI Gateway credits, if they want them. The credits are optional and don't affect the cash sponsorship.

A relationship if you want oneWe're happy to work with maintainers on content, events, integrations, or product feedback when it makes sense for both sides. None of it is a condition of the sponsorship.

sections.heading: How did we get here? Seasons 1 - 8
paragraphs: Season 1 Theme: Genesis and unstructured community grants
Season 2 Theme: Establishing structure with grant committees
Season 3 Theme: Refining structure with the Grants Council
Season 4 Theme: Working as a Collective (Introduction of Missions, Intents, and Trust Tiers)
Season 5 Theme: Governance resiliency (Introduction of the Security Council, Law of Chains, Developer Advisory Board, and Anticapture Commission)
Season 6 Theme: Optimizing to support the Superchain (Streamlining of Mission process and other structures, Blockspace Charters, Superchain grants, Chain Delegation Program)
Season 7 Theme: Shared success (Alignment around singular Intent and common Mission framework, introduction of Success Metrics)
Season 8 Theme: Purpose-built governance (Protocol Upgrades 2.0, ETH Staking, Budget Board)

The evolution of Seasons are based on 100’s of pieces of feedback documented by the Foundation throughout the Season, reports and analysis conducted by the community, periodic feedback surveys, public feedback threads, retrospectives conducted by community representatives, etc.

Season 6 Theme: Optimizing to support the Superchain (Streamlining of Mission process and other structures, Blockspace Charters, Superchain grants, Chain Delegation Program)
Season 7 Theme: Shared success (Alignment around singular Intent and common Mission framework, introduction of Success Metrics)
Season 8 Theme: Purpose-built governance (Protocol Upgrades 2.0, ETH Staking, Budget Board)

sections.heading: Season 9 Theme: From Experiment to Organization
paragraphs: Over the past year, we introduced a refined process for governing the OP Stack (Protocol Upgrades 2.0) aimed at reducing platform risk. Over the next six months, we’ll gradually introduce an updated process for governing the treasury (Capital Allocation 2.0) to prevent short term extraction at the expense of long term innovation (aka enshittification.)

Thanks to the hard work of all contributors of the Collective, we have arrived at an initial design that we believe will allow Optimism to adapt quickly, remain competitive, and avoid the common failure modes of both web 2 and web 3. Over the next few months, we’ll take momentous steps towards solidifying this initial design on our original four-year timeline. The Foundation - with governance oversight - will continue to monitor, refine, and update the design to ensure the Collective continuously adapts, innovates, and evolves over time.

sections.heading: Intents
paragraphs: Intents are high level goals that the entire Collective works towards. We experimented with having the entire Collective rally around Intents in Seasons 4-8. While helpful in clarifying scope for external contributors, we encountered the following challenges:
Our product and strategy is still rapidly evolving in response to customer feedback and market developments, making it unrealistic to commit to a singular focus for 6-12 months
As we reduce the Collective’s dependency on disparate external contributions, it is less meaningful as a strategic alignment tool
As we streamline governance operations, we realized that ratification of the Intent was not an integral, or enforceable, part of the governance surface area
The Foundation will not propose an Intent in Season 9 or future Seasons.

sections.heading: Missions
paragraphs: Collective contributors will continue to work towards pre-determined success metrics by executing Missions. Missions are specific initiatives aimed at making measurable progress towards pre-defined metrics. Missions are clearly scoped, and can be executed by Collective contributors start-to-finish in six months. In Season 9, Missions will be supported by the Governance Fund.

sections.heading: Community-Led Grant Experiments and Contribution Paths
paragraphs: In order to support Optimism’s continued evolution and enterprise strategy, the Foundation believes it is necessary to conclude community-led grant experiments. These experiments have played a critical role in bootstrapping the Collective and have greatly informed the refined design of the capital allocation system. However, community-led capital allocation no longer aligns with our current business or governance strategy (see Season 9: From Experiment to Organization), which also informs our decision to pause the Retro Funding program.

As in a public company, the primary role of governance will be holding OP Labs accountable. Unlike the original vision of DAOs, the role of governance will not be to enable the broader community to drive progress themselves - via capital allocations or open contributions - but rather to empower voters to ensure those entrusted with this responsibility (OP Labs) perform well. See Season 9: From Experiment to Organization for more details.
All Councils will operate as usual through Season 9, according to the Charters approved in Season 8.
The Foundation will propose the dissolution of the Grants Council and Milestones and Metrics Council, subject to governance approval, at the end of Season 9.
The Foundation will not propose any Retro Funding Missions in Season 9 or 10.

The Foundation has also adapted our communty-led approach to support, deprecating the following contribution paths: supNERDs, numbaNERDs, and techNERDs. While we still believe grassroots, community initiatives are valuable, we’ve redirected our focus away from these programs for two key reasons:
Please note that the govNERDs will continue operating as usual through Season 9, at which point we will conduct a retrospective and evaluate ongoing needs.

All contributions to date have been extremely valuable in the development of the Collective. It is only through these contributions that we’ve been able to experiment with different structures, strategies, and governance responsibilities. Each NERD and Council/Board member has been critical in helping the Collective arrive at the clarity needed to design a new, and improved, type of organization to support the Superchain.

name: Open Technology Fund (OTF) – Internet Freedom Fund
description: Provides non-dilutive grant funding for open source tools, circumvention tech, secure communications, and censorship resistance research worldwide.

sections.heading: Internet Freedom Fund
paragraphs: This fund supports innovative internet freedom projects, including technology development, research, digital security projects, and convenings.

sections.heading: About the Internet Freedom Fund
paragraphs: The Internet Freedom Fund is the primary opportunity through which Open Technology Fund supports innovative global internet freedom projects. These projects are focused on technology development and implementation, but can also include applied research, convenings, and digital security projects. See below for more details about each category.
OTF prioritizes projects coming from individuals or organizations who are applying for the first time, identify as under-represented within the field, and address areas that are underfunded.

sections.heading: Application Process and Award Information
paragraphs: Applications to the Fund go through a two-stage application process and are accepted on a rolling basis.
Awards are between $10,000 and $900,000 for up to 24 months. Ideal applicants seek funding between $50,000 and $200,000 for efforts between 6 and 12 months.

Funding awards are performance-based contracts signed directly with the applicant or applicants. Funding is dispersed upon completion of stated objectives, activities, and deliverables per a schedule outlined in the contract. All payments are made in U.S. dollars and will comply with local laws, regulations, and ethics rules.

Successful applicants are paired with an OTF program manager who will oversee all project monitoring and evaluation for the duration of the contract. Monitoring and evaluation assessments are based on predetermined and agreed-upon metrics, deliverables, and goals as laid out by the applicant in the project proposal.

sections.heading: Funding Categories
paragraphs: OTF supports the development of innovative internet freedom technologies from the prototype phase to deployment phase, in addition to supporting core infrastructure projects that serve the internet freedom and human rights communities.
Applications for this category can include, but are not limited to:

OTF supports the applied research efforts of the internet freedom community through the Internet Freedom Fund. This includes research that identifies where and how censorship is occurring, studying the methods to counteract censorship, and advancing knowledge around what types of content is targeted to help assess threats to internet freedom.
Applications for this category can include, but are not limited to:

Authoritarian censors are sharing strategies, techniques and—in some cases—the tools to enact repressive information controls. To effectively counter this highly orchestrated, well-resourced, and pervasive online censorship and surveillance, we need a strong digital security ecosystem that can grow and adapt to evolving threats.

OTF seeks to support systematic improvements to this ecosystem, including infrastructure-wide investments to help practitioners, threat intel researchers, and other community actors make systematic changes to boost the impact of digital security work.

If you have an idea that will support the growth and adaptability of the regional and/or global digital security network, including improving coordination and collaboration—we’d love to hear from you.

Applications in this category should include thoughtful consideration of existing and complementary efforts and a clear explanation of how the proposed effort will lead to positive change in the global and/or regional digital security ecosystem.

Please be mindful that OTF does not support one-off training, training of trainers, or organizational capacity building as an effort’s primary outcome. Various other funders provide these types of direct support for digital security providers.

Note: In some cases, our Rapid Response Fund can support emergency digital security training for at-risk individuals and organizations facing an active or imminent threat, but our digital security support under the Internet Freedom Fund is focused on ecosystem-wide solutions.

OTF provides funding that empowers internet freedom communities to collaborate and work cohesively to improve knowledge sharing and collaboration, cultivate deeper trust, and support and diversify the next generation of Internet freedom leaders. Supported efforts include a wide representation of voices to foster greater collaboration and intersectionality. OTF believes that the need to build a collective vision and strategy with a diverse global network of internet freedom collaborators is becoming increasingly important.
Applications for this category can include, but are not limited to:
bullets: Taking an existing open-source internet freedom technology and improving upon its security, usability, and adaptability
Developing content redistribution methods to aid in content access behind government firewalls
Improving security standards, quality assurance, and best practices within core infrastructure projects
Research that focuses on real-time monitoring and analysis of threats to internet freedom
Research exploring new methods or improvements of censorship circumvention tools
Efforts that increase the understanding and awareness of the Internet freedom community, their roles, and how they contribute to maintaining a free and open internet

User research identifying the needs of people living under repressive surveillance and censorship, how technologies and tools can address those needs, and how these tools can introduce usability and localization improvements
Targeted research and development gatherings designed to improve collaboration and knowledge sharing between projects in the areas of privacy, circumvention technology, and digital security
Community organized events to identify needs, share resources, and gain new insights about censorship, surveillance, and digital security issues

sections.heading: Areas Outside of Our Remit
paragraphs: OTF knows our applicants’ time is valuable so we aim to make our application process as transparent and straightforward as possible. In order to better reflect our respect for an applicant’s time and effort in submitting an application, we have detailed below common types of proposed projects that we are unable or very rarely support. If your project falls within one of these categories, we encourage you to explore our alternative sources of support resources to identify a more suitable funder.

OTF does not provide support for basic connectivity except in limited cases around politically instigated internet shutdowns. Numerous U.S. Government programs outside of OTF provide support for bringing Internet connectivity to areas that have never had it previously. The framework OTF operates within ensures a clear distinction exists to protect against overlapping mandates which is why we do not support projects of this nature.

OTF does not provide support for projects focused on harnessing technology for the purpose of societal development. Numerous U.S. Government programs exist to support civic technology projects that use technology to solve societal challenges, such as improving government delivery of services, providing equitable access to technologies and improving digital literacy across society. The OTF program is focused on assisting those exposed to censorship or surveillance in repressive environments.

OTF does not provide support for projects to improve the legal and policy landscape, outside of narrowly focused technical research to help inform these efforts. Numerous U.S. Government programs provide support for efforts to conduct legal analysis and improve advocacy for specific policies. The framework OTF operates within ensures a clear distinction exists to protect against overlapping mandates. In addition, these types of activities do not reflect the technology-centric approach underlying the OTF program.

sections.heading: How to Apply:
paragraphs: Applying for the Internet Freedom Fund is a two-stage application process:
Stage 1: Submit a Concept Note through OTF’s online application system in which you tell us about your project idea through a short form.
Stage 2: Applicants whose Concept Notes are deemed to be highly competitive will be invited to submit a Proposal in which they will expand upon their project idea

The Internet Freedom Fund Advisory Council, comprising subject-matter experts who understand various relevant fields and issues related to internet freedom, will conduct a final review of competitive Proposals.
Please review our Applicant Guidebook for additional information about our application process, especially the Concept Note Guide and Review Process sections.
The video below guides you through the Concept Note form step-by-step, explaining what we’re looking for under each question.

sections.heading: Application Review Process
paragraphs: Applicants can expect to hear back within approximately 6-8 weeks after submitting a Concept Note.
bullets: Does the proposed effort fit within OTF’s remit?
Does it solve an existing problem (or preempt a rising problem)? What is the real-world applicability of the proposed effort?
Is it sustainable? Will the project survive beyond the life of OTF’s support?

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: Individuals ages 18+ or organizations (for-profit or nonprofit) irrespective of nationality, creed, or sex are eligible to apply.
OTF is not able to support applicants within countries that the United States has trade restrictions or export sanctions as determined by the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).

sections.heading: 👋 Introduction
paragraphs: At the Polymesh Association, we want to improve and extend the Polymesh ecosystem. sections.heading: Guidelines
paragraphs: Anyone is welcome to apply for a grant. Projects funded through our programs are broad in scope, but our focus lies on strong technical projects that add value to the Polymesh ecosystem.
Generally, your project will have better chances to be accepted if:

In addition to the information provided on your application, note that your project will need to comply with our Guidelines for Milestone Deliverables. In particular, we require all projects to create documentation that explains how their project works. At a minimum, written documentation is required for funding. Tutorials or videos are also helpful for new users to understand how to use your product.

Finally, we take licensing and the right of all teams in and outside the ecosystem to be recognised for their work very seriously. Using others' work with no attribution or indication that this was not your own work as part of a milestone delivery will lead to immediate termination. Please reach out to us before submitting if you have any doubts on how to comply with a specific license and we'll be happy to help.
bullets: It presents a well-researched or tested concept, for which ideally you are able to show some prior work.

You can demonstrate that the project will be maintained after completion of the grant, be it through an obvious commitment to the technology from your side, additional funding sources or an existing business model.

Your team has proven experience with the relevant languages and technologies and/or a strong technical background. You will be asked to provide the GitHub profiles of your team members as part of your application, which we will examine these for past activity and code quality. Naturally, you can also link to projects on other platforms.
Your application is rich in technical details and well-defined.
You can clearly present how your project stands out among competitors or implements technology that doesn't exist in the ecosystem yet.

All code produced as part of a grant must be open-sourced, and it must also not rely on closed-source software for full functionality. We prefer Apache 2.0, but GPLv3, MIT or Unlicense are also acceptable.
We do not award grants for projects that have been the object of a successful token sale.
As a general rule, teams are asked to finish a grant before applying for another one.
Lastly, we do not fund projects that actively encourage gambling, illicit trade, money laundering or criminal activities in general.

paragraphs: Requests For Proposals (RFPs) represent concrete ideas for projects that we would like to see implemented and can be a good example of ideas to consider. sections.heading: Support
paragraphs: The scope of our Grants Programs consists of funding and feedback on delivered milestones. This means that we do not provide hands-on support as part of a grant, but if you face specific issues during development, we will do our best and try to direct you to the correct resources. We encourage you to join the community in order to get help with specific issues or to stay up to date with the most recent developments.

sections.heading: 📝 Process
paragraphs: 📢 The process below is independent of the level.

sections.heading: 1. Application
bullets: In the newly created fork, create a copy of the application template (applications/application-template.md). If you're using the GitHub web interface, you will need to create a new file and copy the contents of the template inside the new one. Make sure you do not modify the template file directly.
Name the new file after your project: project_name.md.

Fill out the template with the details of your project. The more information you provide, the faster the review. Please refer to our Grant guidelines for most popular grant categories and make sure your deliverables present a similar same level of detail. Naturally, if you're only applying for a smaller grant that only consists of, say, UI work, you don't need to provide as much detail.
Once you're done, create a pull request. The pull request should only contain one new file—the Markdown file you created from the template.

You will see a comment template that contains a checklist. You can leave it as is and tick the checkboxes once the pull request has been created. Please read through these items and check all of them.
Submitting the Pull Request will mean that you have agreed to the terms and conditions

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: The Prototype Fund is a low-threshold funding program for free developers and small teams who develop innovative Free and Open Source Software from society and for society.

The Prototype Fund is the first low-threshold funding program for independent developers in Germany who develop innovative Free and Open Source Software from society and for society. The measure, also known as “Software Sprint”, has been in place since 2017. The funding program will support software projects on their way from idea to software prototype through 2031. Users are not only consumers of software but often also experts: We use this intersection and offer tech-savvy members of civil society access to the resources and processes they need to contribute to the public good.

We only fund software projects with added social value that focus on the needs of users and are freely available, sustainably accessible and customizable as open source software. There are three funding streams: “Innovation”, “Resilience”, and “Up and Coming”. The “Innovation” track supports projects in the areas of data security and software infrastructure. The “Up and Coming” program focuses on promoting young talent in these fields. The “Resilience” track focuses on decentralized and open alternatives to Big Tech and its centralized ecosystems.

paragraphs: Submit your detailed proposal via the Qubic website (check proposal requirements below).

Proposals are evaluated by the Incubation Board within 1–2 weeks since submission, based on impact, feasibility, and alignment with Qubic goals. AI-assisted writing is acceptable. Vague, padded, and generic writing is not. Every important claim should point to evidence, a decision, or a concrete plan.
The final decision is communicated to the team. If approved, the project can start and you’ll be assigned a project manager as your point of contact.

Projects are delivered in milestones with a QA process executed by Qubic to unlock payment. Qubic pays upon delivery — no upfront payment is made under any circumstances. Milestones must be composed of testable deliverables from a user perspective (documentation, mockups, features…).
If your project includes SC development, Qubic will cover audit costs (1 per project; if more are required the project team assumes the costs).
Once fully delivered, Qubic supports mainnet deployment (if SC involved) and organizes an AMA for engagement purposes.

name: RGB Grants Program
description: RGB Protocol Association is a Swiss non-profit Association that supports the ecosystem, community, and education around RGB Protocol on Bitcoin — the open-source protocol for digital assets and private contracts on Bitcoin and the Lightning Network.

sections.heading: Supporting RGB Protocol on Bitcoin since 2025
paragraphs: RGB Protocol Association is a Swiss non-profit Association that supports the ecosystem, community, and education around RGB Protocol on Bitcoin — the open-source protocol for digital assets and private contracts on Bitcoin and the Lightning Network.

sections.heading: Who we are
paragraphs: RGB Protocol Association was founded in July 2025 in Switzerland as a non-profit Association under Articles 60–79 of the Swiss Civil Code. It was created to provide institutional support for RGB Protocol on Bitcoin and the broader ecosystem of open-source projects building on it.

The Association is composed of corporate members — companies, organizations, and engineering teams active in the Bitcoin and RGB ecosystem. Strategic direction is set by a board elected by the General Assembly of members.
We do not maintain or develop the RGB protocol. We support those who do.

sections.heading: What we do
paragraphs: Three pillars define how the Association supports RGB Protocol on Bitcoin.

sections.heading: Ecosystem
paragraphs: We back independent developers, engineering teams, and infrastructure projects building on RGB Protocol on Bitcoin. This includes wallets, libraries, node implementations, and tooling that expand what is possible to build on the protocol.We work with builders across the open-source community — those already shipping production-grade work, and those bringing new ideas and technical proposals to the ecosystem.

sections.heading: Community
paragraphs: We organize and sponsor events, workshops, meetups, and conferences that bring together developers, researchers, and builders working on RGB and adjacent open-source systems on Bitcoin.These activities exist online and in person — from technical gatherings to international conferences — with the aim of strengthening the connections that hold the ecosystem together.

sections.heading: Education
paragraphs: We promote educational initiatives, hackathons, and learning programs that introduce developers and builders to RGB Protocol on Bitcoin. The goal is to lower the entry barrier and grow the next generation of contributors to the ecosystem.This includes technical workshops, in-person and online hackathons, and partnerships with educational platforms that cover Bitcoin development at large.

sections.heading: What we are not
paragraphs: RGB Protocol on Bitcoin is open-source software. Like any open-source protocol, it belongs to no one. Anyone can read the code, propose changes, build on top of it, or contribute independently.

The Association does not develop the protocol — that work is done by the rgb-protocol team. The Association does not govern the protocol — open-source software has no central authority. We exist to support the ecosystem with community work, educational initiatives, and infrastructure for the people building on RGB Protocol on Bitcoin, and we encourage every developer to contribute on their own terms.

sections.heading: Become part of the ecosystem
paragraphs: We welcome conversations with organizations, builders, and partners working on Bitcoin, the Lightning Network, and adjacent open-source systems.

name: SafePal x Solana Builder Grant
description: Today, we’re excited to announce the launch of the SafePal Solana Builders Grant, a $3 million initiative designed to help Solana ecosystem projects and builders scale sustainably throughout 2026.

sections.heading: SafePal Builder’s Grant: $3 Million Solana Ecosystem Growth Initiative
paragraphs: Today, we’re excited to announce the launch of the SafePal Solana Builders Grant, a $3 million initiative designed to help Solana ecosystem projects and builders scale sustainably throughout 2026.
Since 2021, SafePal has integrated the Solana network and supported the ecosystem by supporting and implementing important features for users. Recent and existing features include:

-A dedicated Solana DeFi hub in SafePal’s mobile and hardware wallets-Native support to buy, swap, trade, and stake $SOL and SPL tokens-Access to emerging verticals such as tokenized stocks and other trending on-chain assets

While user needs and security has always been a key priority for SafePal, long-term and meaningful Web3 growth also comes from empowering other builders with the right tools to better serve users. The success of pilot Walletdrop campaigns with DeFi protocols such as Jumper Exchange, 1inch, and Morpho have proven that growth strategies focused on ownership, security, and real users outperform hype-driven approaches, serving as a strong impetus for the creation of a larger scale initiative and launch of the grant.
The grant program will run across the full year of 2026 and consists of:

sections.heading: 1. $2 million worth of SafePal hardware wallet sponsorships: a meaningful and effective growth mechanism:
paragraphs: As the crypto industry matures, more innovative projects are emerging especially on high-activity ecosystems like Solana. However, teams still struggle with sustainable and relevant user growth.

Token airdrops are widely used, but they often create short-lived momentum, attract mercenary users and bots, and sometimes divert focus away from long-term product value and finding actual product market fit.
Hardware Walletdrops offer a different path, offering stronger user retention, higher-quality engagement, and significantly less bot abuse.

While initiatives like InfoFi have emerged to offer channels for projects to build rich and engaging users, the accuracy, effectiveness and sustainability remain inconsistent. Projects and builders still need cost-efficient, high-impact growth tools that deliver meaningful and relevant results.This section of the grant will offer resources to boost user retention and brand image, such as premium listings in the SafePal Dapp center and homepage, the opportunity to collaborate and create in-depth customized tasks to drive actual product usage and track conversions, filtering relevant users by whitelisting based on asset and behavior to combat bot farmers and more.Solana ecosystem projects can apply for the grant via the official SafePal website here.

Applications will be evaluated based on criteria such as the length of time the project has been live, monthly active users (MAU), total value locked (TVL), community size and engagement, ecosystem contributions (e.g. hackathons, workshops, developer events), and more.

sections.heading: Commemorating the grant launch: Limited-Edition Solana x SafePal Hardware Wallets
paragraphs: To commemorate the launch of the grant, SafePal has produced 1,500 limited-edition Solana branded hardware wallets. These wallets will be distributed during Solana Accelerate APAC to event attendees, VIPs and core contributors, and also via selected bounty and community programs thereafter.

SafePal will also be exploring future potential additional utilities for these wallets, including staking benefits and airdrop boosts for this exclusive collection and for wallets distributed through the grant program.

Looking ahead, SafePal will continue supporting the Solana ecosystem together with other blockchain ecosystems and crypto protocols as part of our roadmap to evolve into a comprehensive DeFi and CeFi hub while staying true to our mission of secure, user-first self-custody.

paragraphs: Founded in 2018, SafePal is a next generation non-custodial crypto wallet suite backed by Animoca Brands, Binance and Superscrypt. The suite empowers access to decentralized and centralized finance on 200+ blockchains across its hardware, software, and browser extension wallet solutions.

Encompassing a diverse mix of crypto asset management solutions like cross-chain swapping, trading and yielding tools, centralized exchange (CEX) mini programs, a banking gateway and Mastercard for users — SafePal serves 30 million users globally across 200+ regions and countries in 16 languages.
