name: Scaleup Europe Fund
description:
The European Commission has completed the final legal steps required to establish the Scaleup Europe Fund, a major new investment initiative designed to help Europe’s most promising technology companies grow into global market leaders.

With a target size of €5 billion, the Fund will invest directly in European scaleups operating in strategic technology sectors. Its first investments are expected to take place in the coming weeks.

sections.heading: Europe’s new multi-billion late-stage and growth Fund to invest in our most promising, strategic companies
paragraphs: The Scaleup Europe Fund is a new, multi-billion late-stage and growth fund aimed at investing in the most promising European companies in strategic tech areas, such as artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, semiconductor technologies, robotics and autonomous systems, energy technologies, space technologies, biotechnologies, medical technologies, advanced materials, and agritech, and across all parts of Europe.
The Scaleup Europe Fund responds to the urgent need for Europe to boost investments in scaleups and close the gap with global leaders.

sections.heading: Powered by Europe’s top investors
paragraphs: The new Scaleup Europe Fund brings new momentum to Europe’s scaleup ecosystem, anchored in public-private cooperation.

Alongside the Commission, the group of founding investors in the Fund include Novo Holdings, EIFO (Export and Investment Fund of Denmark), CriteriaCaixa, Santander/Mouro Capital, Fondazione Compagnia San Paolo/ Intesa Sanpaolo/Fondazione Cariplo, APG Asset Management, acting on behalf of Dutch pension fund ABP, Wallenberg Investments and Allianz.
The Fund will be part of the existing EIC Fund umbrella structure but with a fully privately owned and market-based fund manager.

The fund is a key initiative of the EU Startup and Scaleup Strategy, announced by Commission President Ursula von der Leyen in her 2025 State of the Union Address, aimed at making major investments in fast-growing companies in strategic tech areas, so that "the best of Europe can choose Europe".
Call for expression of interest for the Fund Manager - results announced

The European Innovation Council (EIC) Fund Board has chosen EQT as the preferred investment adviser and fund manager for the Scaleup Europe Fund, following a rigorous and highly competitive selection process to lead the EU's €5 billion initiative designed to empower the continent's most innovative deep tech scaleups.
The Scaleup Europe Fund and its fund manager were presented at the EIC Summit on 3 June 2026 and has made its first investments in summer 2026.

sections.heading: General
paragraphs: Despite Europe's thriving startup ecosystem, many innovative European companies face significant challenges in accessing the capital they need to scale up and become global leaders in Europe.

Currently, there is no fund of comparable size that provides direct equity investments in European strategic technology companies at the growth and scaleup stages, forcing many to seek funding outside of Europe.

The Scaleup Europe Fund addresses this critical gap, by providing a much-needed source of capital to support the growth of Europe's most promising technology companies in major, European-led funding rounds.

EQT was selected as preferred Fund Manager following a competitive public call for expressions of interest. EQT, a leading global private markets firm with a strong track record in growth and technology investing, will operate as an independent, market-based fund manager, ensuring professional and commercially-driven investment decision-making.

The European Commission is a founding investor of the Scaleup Europe Fund, alongside other private investors. As such, the European Commission will participate on equal terms with the other investors and have a corresponding representation in the Fund's governance structure.
The European Commission has committed to contribute EUR 1 billion to the fund.

With EQT introduced as the Fund Manager and the Scaleup Europe Fund publicly launched at the EIC Summit on 3 June 2026, the focus has now moved to finalizing the Fund’s legal and governance structure. This involves completing the legal documentation with the founding investors, with the aim of reaching a first closing as soon as possible. EQT will subsequently lead a second fundraising round to broaden the investor base. First investments of the fund in European deep tech companies, are expected to follow shortly after the first closing.

The Scaleup Europe Fund is a concrete delivery of the European Commission’s Competitiveness Compass and a direct response to the Draghi Report’s call for Europe to close its deep-tech financing gap. The SEF combines private and public funding to support European companies through a market-based approach, without controlling market outcomes.

sections.heading: Targeted at companies
paragraphs: The Fund is now in the process of completing its legal setup ahead of the first closing. Once operational, EQT will be responsible for managing the full investment process, including deal sourcing and company
selection. The selection of investee companies will be conducted through an open, transparent, and merit-based process in line with the Investment Guidelines.

Further details on the investment process will be communicated by EQT once the Fund is operational. While prior participation in EIC instruments may be relevant, it will not confer any preferential treatment.
More information will be published, as soon as available, at: scaleupeuropefund.eu

The Fund will be open to companies located in or intending to locate to any EU Member State or countries associated with Pillar III of Horizon Europe, which are developing strategic technologies and seeking major investment amounts in growth and scaleup stages.
The initial investments are expected in the autumn of 2026, shortly after the founding investors closing.
Going forward, EQT will lead engagement with potential investee companies as part of its deal sourcing activities. Relevant events where EQT are present can also be found on the EIC website.

The Scaleup Europe Fund aims to provide investments beyond what the EIC currently offers, which is limited to EUR 30 million under the EIC STEP call. The Scaleup Europe Fund will have no formal or mandatory linkage to the EIC portfolio. However, the current EIC Fund portfolio may serve as a potential pipeline for the fund manager.

By providing access to significant capital to companies at growth and scaleup stage (in the range of EUR 100 million and above – including follow-on investments), the Scaleup Europe Fund will enable European companies to grow into competitive, global leaders.
This, in turn, will benefit both innovators and investors, as Europe's pipeline of highly innovative startup companies offers attractive investment opportunities.

The Fund will also help address the increasing dominance of foreign investors in large funding rounds, thereby reducing risks such as strategic dependency, company relocation, foreign control, and talent outflow.

The Fund will focus on European companies developing strategic technologies, including but not limited to: deep tech, life sciences, clean tech, advanced manufacturing, and digital technologies. The specific investment strategy and sector focus will be developed by EQT in line with the Fund’s Investment Guidelines. The Fund is designed to be technology-forward and flexible, and will be able to back Europe’s most promising scaleup companies across a range of strategic sectors.

sections.heading: Targeted at investors
paragraphs: The founding investors of the Scaleup Europe Fund are Novo Holdings, EIFO (Export and Investment Fund of Denmark), Criteria Caixa, Santander/Mouro Capital, Fondazione Compagnia di San Paolo/Intesa Sanpaolo/Fondazione Cariplo, ABP represented by APG as its Asset Manager, and Alliance e, that are European leading pension funds, venture capital, investment and asset management companies, and the European Commission. Together, the founding investors bring significant capital as well as deep strategic and institutional expertise to the Fund.
The founding investors will join the European Commission in the first closing of the Fund, with opportunities for additional investors to join later on.

After the first closing of the fund, a second fundraising round will be launched to diversify and expand the investor base. This will allow additional investors to join the Fund, including possibly non-European investors aligned with the SEF objectives, while maintaining strong European anchoring within the investor base.
Institutional investors and foundations that share the objectives of SEF, to retain strategic assets in Europe and create a sustainable deep-tech ecosystem.

The founding investors are key partners in the launch of the Scaleup Europe Fund. They comprise private investors, foundations, pension funds and more. The group of founding investors, besides the European Commission, were selected based on their interest to make a significant capital investment and to contribute expertise to developing the Fund.

They also align with the strategic vision of the Scaleup Europe Fund to invest at European level in a multi-billion euro growth and late-stage fund to target the investment opportunities stemming from Europe's pipeline of excellent technology companies, as the same time as they contribute to retain strategic assets in Europe and create a sustainable deep-tech ecosystem.

EQT was selected through a competitive, open public call for expressions of interest, which closed on 3 February 2026. The selection was based on EQT’s strong track record in growth and technology investing, its European anchoring, its ability to raise additional private capital, and its capacity to manage a fund of the SEF’s ambition and scale. The selection was confirmed by the EIC Fund Board on 18 May 2026 and publicly announced at the EIC Summit on 3 June 2026.

The Scaleup Europe Fund targets a total size of approximately EUR 5 billion, anchored by EUR 1 billion contribution from the European Commission. The founding investors are contributing alongside the European Commission in the first closing, with EQT expected to lead a second fundraising to further scale the fund towards its target size.

EQT will manage the Scaleup Europe Fund as an independent, market-based investment manager. All investment decisions will be made by EQT on commercial and merit-based grounds, in line with the Fund’s Investment Guidelines. The European Commission and other investors will participate in governance structures as investors but will not direct individual investment decisions. This separation is fundamental to ensuring the Fund operates with the credibility and agility required to compete effectively in the market.

name: Sentient Foundation Open Source AGI Grant Program
provider: Sentient Foundation Open Source AGI Grant Program
description: Sentient Foundation, a nonprofit aiming to support open, decentralized artificial general intelligence (AGI), announced a $42M grant program.

sections.heading: The Most Important Technology Ever Built Is Being Locked Behind Closed Doors.
paragraphs: We are funding the builders who will keep it open.

A few companies are tightening their grip on humanity's most important technology. Access is metered, priced to climb, and revocable overnight. A developer in Lagos, Bangalore, or São Paulo can lose the model their work depends on without warning.
The Sentient Foundation is backing the developers building AI in the open, and the products that put it in the hands of the people the market has always skipped.
No equity. No lockups. No claim on your work.Just build.

sections.heading: Why Now
paragraphs: For two years, open models trailed the closed ones by a wide margin, and it was easy to call the open bet the idealistic one. That gap has nearly closed. Open models are now within striking distance of the frontier. ‍The question is no longer whether we can build in the open. It is who gets there first. If closed labs set the defaults, they get set behind glass: metered, surveilled, revocable, shaped for whoever pays most. If open builders win the race, the default flips because open weights, once released, can never be taken back. That’s the window. It is open now, and it does not stay open. We are funding the people who move through it.

sections.heading: Open
paragraphs: Anyone can run it, inspect it, and build on it, and that is why it works.

sections.heading: Yours to keep
paragraphs: A tool you can be cut off from was never yours, and open weights, once released, can never be taken back.

sections.heading: Accessible
paragraphs: It runs on the hardware people actually own, because the cheapest phone is the only computer most of the world has.

sections.heading: Good for humanity
paragraphs: It makes real life measurably better, especially for those the market overlooked.

sections.heading: Private by default
paragraphs: The most sensitive data never leaves the person's own device.

sections.heading: Empowering, not extractive
paragraphs: It hands people a capability, instead of harvesting them for one.

description: Shift grants aim to bridge funding gaps for d/acc. The current paradigm prioritizes short-term returns, leaving defensive and decentralized innovations underfunded. We want to address this.

sections.heading: What are Shift Grants
paragraphs: Shift grants aim to bridge funding gaps for d/acc.
The current paradigm prioritizes short-term returns, leaving defensive and decentralized innovations underfunded. We want to address this.
We aim to direct philanthropic funding through small and development grants in six domains: Biosecurity, Cyber Defense, Info Resilience, Infrastructure, NeuroTech, Social Tech/Governance.

sections.heading: Genesis Cohort: Meet the First Shift Grantees
paragraphs: Nine teams turning the d/acc ethos—decentralised, democratic, differential, defensive acceleration—into code, hardware, and systems.
9 breakthrough projects that make up our Genesis Cohort:

A cross-disciplinary task force (AI-lab security, hardware, national-security) that will publish a step-by-step roadmap—and early prototypes—needed for “SL5” model-weight security. Today’s best AI labs top out at “Security Level 3.” That stops casual hackers, but not a well-resourced nation state. The SL5 Task Force convenes data-centre operators, cyber-officers, and ML researchers to draft the first action-plan for truly top-shelf AI security—then prototypes hardware and software fixes labs can adopt right away.

End-to-end encryption is great—until you need to share a file. dCypher ships an open-source re-encryption proxy that lets you hand temporary, revocable access to any piece of data while it stays encrypted on disk. Built on lattice-based (post-quantum) crypto and designed for a one-command cloud deploy. Think “Dropbox-style sharing,” but encrypted, with the possibility to grant or revoke access instantly.

An onchain, open-source, token-agnostic prediction market for surfacing trustworthy, future-focused insights. Goal is to enable communities (e.g. Zu Nodes) to coordinate around real signals rather than noise. Accurate forecasters earn reputation and rewards; AI agents can read the ledger to update their own models.

Replacing centralized communication in robotics with a peer-to-peer, libp2p-based middleware for ROS 2. Most robots speak ROS2, but its networking assumes every bot lives on the same trusted LAN. This project swaps in libp2p’s peer-to-peer mesh, letting robots from different vendors coordinate in warehouses, farms, or disaster zones without a shared cloud account. Enables secure, cross-fleet communication among autonomous systems—goal is resilient, cross-vendor robotic infrastructure.
Decentralizing emergency blood donation infrastructure in rural Bangladesh. Combines AI urgency scoring, open-source platforms, and low-literacy tools to ensure blood access.

Developing a biocomputation platform using 3D-bioprinted neural tissues to perform programmable computation. Merging living neurons with silicon for next-generation brain-machine interfaces and bioartificial intelligence. Intactis grows thumbnail-sized neural tissues, trains them, and connects them to silicon control circuits—a first step toward low-energy bio-computers.

Designs personalized neural tissue using multimodal AI and digital twin simulations—enabling low-cost, high-fidelity neural grafts for cognitive repair and progressive brain replacement. Eightsix feeds MRI scans into a multimodal LLM, simulates the print-and-grow cycle entirely in software, then outputs a ready-to-print scaffold.
An AI-assisted governance system tailored to pop-up cities. Combines "broad listening," configurable AI representatives, and quadratic voting to strengthen participatory decision-making.

A non-profit quantum computing initiative to establish an open-source quantum ecosystem. Quantum computing risks becoming proprietary before it’s useful. unitaryFoundation Keeps quantum computing in the commons.

sections.heading: Grant Types
paragraphs: Micro Grants ($5,000–$15,000) For exploratory ideas, early-stage experiments, and prototype development.
Applicants should clearly articulate their concept, d/acc alignment, and preliminary plan. Deliverables can be simple but must be concrete.

Development Grants ($20,000–$40,000) For teams with the capacity to execute and deliver measurable milestones. Applicants must provide a roadmap, define technical and execution risks, and commit to iterative reporting and engagement.
Follow-on funding may be considered for outstanding projects.

sections.heading: Selection Criteria
paragraphs: Proposals must clearly engage with at least three of the four “d”s. If one "d" is absent, applicants must explain why this is consistent with the spirit of d/acc. If a proposal conflicts with a pillar (e.g., private biosecurity R&D), justification must be compelling.

Open-source dissemination is the default. Security-sensitive work must include mitigation strategies and a justification for any elements of the project that are not open-sourced. Ethical implications should be considered explicitly.
Strong preference for ideas that could shift paradigms or form the basis of new fields.
Clear plans and realistic milestones are required. Development proposals must show technical depth and real-world applicability.
Confidence in the Team Track record is less important than clarity of vision and fit.

paragraphs: Sign up here to stay informed about when Shift Grants Round 003 opens

For the 002 round of funding, the process was:
The totality of the applications are triaged and shortlisted by the Shift core team and advisors
Final fund distribution is decided by the advisory board.
Evaluation methods may differ in future rounds based on community feedback and performance.

sections.heading: Grant Administration
paragraphs: The current paradigm prioritizes short-term returns, leaving defensive and decentralized innovations underfunded. We want to address this. Our long-term vision is a sustainable, revolving funding model. When grantees develop revenue, they're invited to return value back into the fund. This system enable the next wave of d/acc-aligned innovation and creates a self-sustaining engine for collective progress.

paragraphs: The Shutter DAO 0x36 Impact Pilot is a two-round program that rewards demonstrated value to Shutter—not titles, affiliation, time spent, or ideas alone.

Round 1 funds defined, reviewable work that advances a concrete Shutter need, opportunity, or gap. Applicants should identify the relevant people or organizations where applicable, define a practical deliverable, and show what the work will help someone decide or do next.
Read the Impact Pilot Program discussion before applying.
Expected Round 1 awards: 2–4 grants, generally in the $1,000–$3,000 range
Unspent funds: Any unused Round 1 funds will roll into Round 2 and be reported publicly
bullets: Expected Round 1 awards: 2–4 grants, generally in the $1,000–$3,000 range
Unspent funds: Any unused Round 1 funds will roll into Round 2 and be reported publicly

sections.heading: Commercial standard
paragraphs: A contribution does not need to produce revenue during the grant period.

However, it must produce evidence that moves a defined Shutter opportunity forward. Show the need, the relevant Shutter capability, who needs to be involved, and the next step toward use, funding, or deployment.

sections.heading: Objective 1: Qualify an Encrypted-Transaction Deployment Opportunity
paragraphs: The encrypted mempool is Shutter’s crypto infrastructure project. Pending transactions normally sit in a public mempool where anyone can read them before they execute, which enables front-running, sandwich attacks, and censorship. Shutter encrypts transactions until the moment they are included in a block, so nobody can see or exploit them while they wait.

Identify and qualify a concrete opportunity for Shutter’s encrypted-mempool integration with a wallet, dApp, RPC provider, routing service, chain, validator ecosystem, or other transaction-flow operator.
Deliver a scoped assessment, pilot proposal, or feasibility test tied to a named operator (or a substantiated route to one), a defined transaction flow, and a stated next decision.
Generic outreach, contact lists, and generic explainers do not qualify.
bullets: Identify and qualify a concrete opportunity for Shutter’s encrypted-mempool integration with a wallet, dApp, RPC provider, routing service, chain, validator ecosystem, or other transaction-flow operator.
Deliver a scoped assessment, pilot proposal, or feasibility test tied to a named operator (or a substantiated route to one), a defined transaction flow, and a stated next decision.

sections.heading: Objective 2: Qualify a Private Voting Deployment
paragraphs: For DAOs and onchain governance: Shutter adds private voting to the platforms and tools they already vote with. Ballots stay encrypted while the vote runs, so voters cannot be pressured, bought, or bandwagoned mid-vote. Results are revealed when the vote closes, or ballots stay secret permanently with only the result published.
For real-world voting: associations, municipalities, and other organizations use Shutter Governance to run private and verifiable elections.
Identify and qualify a concrete opportunity for an existing voting platform to integrate Shutter’s private voting solution.
Deliver a pilot proposal tied to a named platform or body, what they would pay (an integration fee or transaction revenue), and a stated next decision.
Generic advocacy or unsupported interest does not qualify.
Coming Soon to DAOs: Permanent Shielded Voting via Homomorphic Encryption
bullets: Identify and qualify a concrete opportunity for an existing voting platform to integrate Shutter’s private voting solution.
Deliver a pilot proposal tied to a named platform or body, what they would pay (an integration fee or transaction revenue), and a stated next decision.
Coming Soon to DAOs: Permanent Shielded Voting via Homomorphic Encryption

sections.heading: Objective 3: Identify and Validate a Concorde Use Case
paragraphs: Concorde lets a group operate with a shared AI agent that works for the whole group rather than any one member. It can collect input from members, maintain shared history and context, coordinate recurring work, and help groups make and track decisions.
Identify and validate a high-value, repeatable use case and customer segment where a Concorde shared agent could provide meaningful value to the user and generate revenue.

Deliver a decision-ready opportunity assessment based on real user or customer evidence, including the problem, current workflow, required Concorde capabilities, commercial or adoption path, and a proposed route to a first pilot.
Generic market research, lists of possible industries, unsupported use-case ideas, and generic outreach do not qualify.
bullets: Identify and validate a high-value, repeatable use case and customer segment where a Concorde shared agent could provide meaningful value to the user and generate revenue.

Deliver a decision-ready opportunity assessment based on real user or customer evidence, including the problem, current workflow, required Concorde capabilities, commercial or adoption path, and a proposed route to a first pilot.

sections.heading: Objective 4: Validate a Shutter Use Case in Tokenized Markets
paragraphs: Tokenized markets bring stocks, funds, credit, and other assets on chain. Shutter may be useful where revealing orders, allocations, or terms too early creates avoidable execution or coordination risk.

Test a defined use case in tokenized equities, funds, credit, or other real-world-asset workflows where Shutter could address information leakage, allocation fairness, confidential coordination, sealed bidding, or timed disclosure.
Identify the operator, workflow, constraints, and next decision.
Generic market reports and speculative “RWA + privacy” concepts do not qualify.
bullets: Test a defined use case in tokenized equities, funds, credit, or other real-world-asset workflows where Shutter could address information leakage, allocation fairness, confidential coordination, sealed bidding, or timed disclosure.
Identify the operator, workflow, constraints, and next decision.

sections.heading: Objective 5: Package a Repeatable Shutter Workflow
paragraphs: Turn an existing Shutter capability into a reusable workflow for a defined user, operator, or customer segment—for example sealed RFPs, selection processes, procurement, auctions, bug bounties, confidential coordination, or timed disclosure.
Generic demos and unmaintained tooling do not qualify.
bullets: Deliver a productized design, customer- or partner-informed pilot package, or reusable implementation guide.

name: Solana Foundation Grants & Funding
description: The Solana Foundation Funding Program aims to connect builders, creators, and founders to the best source of funding for their work. This may be through the Solana Foundation or other ecosystem sources.

sections.heading: Types of Funding
paragraphs: The Solana Foundation Funding Program aims to connect builders, creators, and founders to the best source of funding for their work. This may be through the Solana Foundation or other ecosystem sources.

sections.heading: Solana Foundation Funding
paragraphs: In the Solana ecosystem’s open-source spirit, the Solana Foundation supports projects that generate public goods for the community and give other ecosystem participants the opportunity to learn from and build on your work.
The Solana Foundation primarily provides funding in the following ways:
bullets: Milestone-based convertible grants for public goods with a commercial component
Requests for Proposals (RFPs) for specific ideas the Foundation is looking to fund

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Please note that the following are a set of guidelines for the Solana Foundation funding application only. Ecosystem sources of funding may have different processes.

sections.heading: Application
paragraphs: All funding applicants for Solana Foundation standard and convertible grants are required to fill out the application here.
bullets: Clarify how your project provides a public good for the Solana network
Lay out a well structured budget proposal, and include thoughtful milestones

sections.heading: Application Review (~1 week)
paragraphs: All applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

If an application warrants an in-depth review, Solana Foundation subject-matter experts (“SME”) will reach out to schedule a call. The due diligence process can include technical due diligence, market research, and other analyses to determine the project’s fit and usefulness to the Solana ecosystem.

sections.heading: Decision & Contacting (~3 weeks)
paragraphs: Applicants will be notified via the email provided in their application whether their proposal has been accepted or not.
Approved applicants work with the Solana Foundation Legal Team to finalize the grant agreement.

sections.heading: Guidelines for Evaluation
paragraphs: While the Solana Foundation appreciates a broad diversity of ideas in grant applications, there are a few common threads that the team always looks for.

We typically consider a project to be a public good if it either makes a significant open-source contribution to the Solana ecosystem, or if it has a meaningful free community offering. Depending on the circumstances, we may also consider a novel proof of concept to qualify. Projects that are primarily commercial in nature usually won’t qualify for a standard grant from the Solana Foundation, and should consider a convertible grant.

Not all projects require code, but they should be built in the spirit of open-sourcing your learnings for everyone to learn from. Projects should benefit the community at large, and while not all parts of the project should be open source, the usable parts should be available to all.

The proposal should make it clear why the project is building within the Solana ecosystem, as opposed to other places or other ways. Why Solana? How does the Solana protocol help the team or project achieve its goals in ways that are not possible elsewhere?

We encourage you to be thoughtful about how much you’re requesting and present a clear plan for how the funding will help you accomplish your goals. Set clear, measurable funding milestones, and make sure the funding you request is correlated to the impact to the community your project is providing.
Please note that this criteria list is not exhaustive, and grant approvals are at the discretion of the Solana Foundation Capital Team.

name: Solana Scholars
description: Solana Scholars builds a bridge between Solana and the academic community. Offering scoped, well-defined 3-month research internships, pairing each scholar directly with the engineers and researchers working on those problems.

sections.heading: Do research
paragraphs: Solana Scholars · Q. Kniep & R. Wattenhofer

Solana Scholars builds a bridge between Solana and the academic community. We fund focused research internships carried out in close collaboration with the people building the system. Your work doesn't end at a PDF. It ends up in production. We put the ship in internship.

sections.heading: Why this program exists
paragraphs: A lot of blockchain research never touches a real system, and a lot of real systems never benefit from research. We think that's a waste in both directions. Solana runs at a scale where open problems in consensus, networking, cryptography, and economics aren't hypothetical — they're on the roadmap.

So we're offering scoped, well-defined 3-month research internships, pairing each scholar directly with the engineers and researchers working on those problems. Internships are on-site — for example in Zurich, Switzerland or New York, USA — or virtual. Every topic is chosen because we genuinely want the answer.

sections.heading: Real problems
paragraphs: Internship topics come from what the system actually needs next — not from a grab bag of "interesting directions."

sections.heading: Close collaboration
paragraphs: You work directly with Solana engineers and researchers throughout the internship, not just at kickoff and final report.

sections.heading: Publishable results
paragraphs: Internships are scoped so the outcome fits your PhD: papers, artifacts, and results you can build a thesis chapter on.

sections.heading: Impact you can point to
paragraphs: The best outcome of an internship is code, protocol changes, or analysis the ecosystem actually uses. That's the bar.

sections.heading: On-site or virtual
paragraphs: Join us in person — for example in Zurich, Switzerland or New York, USA — or work with us remotely from wherever your PhD keeps you.

sections.heading: Built around your PhD
paragraphs: Internships run for 3 months, with a possible extension. Timing is flexible and applications are open year-round, so it fits your program instead of interrupting it.

sections.heading: Who can apply
paragraphs: Right now, the program is open exclusively to _excellent PhD students_. If you're currently enrolled in a doctoral program and work in distributed systems, networking, cryptography, economics, or a neighboring field, we'd love to hear from you.

We expect candidates to have already published at scientific conferences in the area — at venues such as FC, AFT, PODC, DISC, SOSP, OSDI, EuroSys, SIGCOMM, NSDI, SIGMETRICS, CCS, S&P, USENIX Security, NDSS, CRYPTO, EUROCRYPT, EC, or WINE.
You're a great fit if you want your research to run against a real, live, planet-scale distributed system — and you're excited by the idea that a good result doesn't just get cited, it gets deployed.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: Applications are short — we care about your ideas and your fit, not paperwork. Pitch your own topic or express interest in one of our areas; if there's a fit, we scope the internship together. There is no application deadline: we accept applications throughout the year. Whenever you're ready, we're ready.

name: Sovereign Tech Fund (STF)
provider: German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs
description: Sustainable public funding strengthening critical open source digital infrastructure, libraries, foundational protocols, and digital commons.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: We are securing open digital infrastructure as the foundation for a future-oriented economy and modern society

Digital sovereignty empowers us to shape our own future. This requires more than simply using digital technologies; we need to actively be part of building them - to be independent, secure, and competitive.

The foundation for this is open digital infrastructure. Much like roads and railways serve as physical infrastructure, invisible software components are the bedrock of our economy and society. Components like programming libraries, open standards, and developer tools are essential for innovation and competition.

Digital infrastructure emerges from an open source ecosystem that makes it possible to reuse, quickly distribute, and maintain digital technologies. Sustaining this ecosystem protects Germany's and Europe's digital sovereignty, capacity for innovation, and economic competitiveness today and in the future.

sections.heading: Strategic investments in the digital infrastructure of our economy and society
paragraphs: With the Sovereign Tech Fund, we invest globally in the open software components that underpin Germany's and Europe's competitiveness and ability to innovate. By targeting core digital infrastructure, our investments scale across many sectors and benefit a broad range of users. Improving the security, stability, and reusability of open software components directly enhances the productivity, competitive edge, and capacity for innovation of startups and small and medium-sized businesses.

sections.heading: Bug bounty, prevention, and elimination of vulnerabilities in critical digital infrastructure
paragraphs: The Sovereign Tech Resilience program takes a holistic approach to protecting critical digital infrastructure. Severe vulnerabilities in open software components have far-reaching consequences, affecting millions of people and impacting software products of all kinds that make use of them. To mitigate these risks and prevent untold damage, it is not enough just to find and fix bugs. We need to take proactive measures to improve the resilience of open digital infrastructure in the face of undiscovered vulnerabilities.

sections.heading: Effective support for essential experts in the open source ecosystem
paragraphs: Our fellowship program supports key individuals and strengthens the open source ecosystem in a way that transcends individual technologies and industries. By focusing on the people behind the code, we highlight and provide recognition for the often invisible work that goes into our digital infrastructure. In this way, we are empowering more people to put their skills and experience toward making the open source ecosystem more resilient and sustainable for us all.

sections.heading: Interoperability in the open source ecosystem
paragraphs: Open standards determine how software interoperates, how data flows, and how secure and accessible our digital infrastructure is. Yet the open source maintainers who implement these standards are rarely part of the processes that produce them. Participating at IETF, W3C, and ISO takes time, expertise, and resources. The Sovereign Tech Standards network closes that gap by supporting open source maintainers' engagement in standards work, bringing implementation experience into the room where critical decisions about interoperability are made.

sections.heading: New solutions for structural challenges in the open source ecosystem
paragraphs: The Sovereign Tech Challenge uses a competition model to identify challenges in the open source ecosystem and develop new and innovative solutions. Examples of potential objectives could include developing forward-looking solutions in open software components that are useful for emerging technologies, or securing existing dependencies.

name: Spiral Grants
description: Spiral provides grants to projects and individual contributors around the world to help achieve our mission of making sure that money and intelligence become lasting, open source public goods.

sections.heading: We want to fund you.
paragraphs: Spiral provides grants to projects and individual contributors around the world to help achieve our mission of making sure that money and intelligence become lasting, open source public goods.
We cast a wide net for non-commercial projects that will have significant long-term impact on either the open source AI ecosystem or bitcoin—maybe even both.
If you have a big idea in mind, go ahead and Apply Now by sending us a detailed proposal.
If you're looking for inspiration, here are some areas of work that we think are, and will continue to be, important:
Spiral is especially interested in funding projects that make open source AI:

More useful. How can open models—and the related tooling, agents and apps in the open ecosystem—win over closed alternatives? We’d love to see open local models be more efficient, more private, more powerful for specific uses (like scientific research) and more broadly accessible, especially in constrained environments like mobile and embedded hardware. We’re also excited by novel approaches to training, fine-tuning and reinforcement learning that push the capabilities of open models forward. Everything that makes open the better option for builders, for users, for the world.

More open. How does open intelligence currently fall short of being fully open? For one, we think more open-weight models should be fully open source, so we need open data provenance and training methods. Benchmarking should be more open, non-gameable, transparent and reproducible. Open APIs should become so universal they become standards that closed labs can’t not support. And we need to preserve access to data and services for open source agents on the open web.

More secure. What can the open source community do to ensure open intelligence helps keep us safe without compromising freedom? Fundamentally, privacy is core to user safety: as AI becomes more deeply embedded in our lives, we need stronger guarantees that our personal information, private conversations and sensitive data are protected from exposure and misuse. More broadly we think the answer will come from greater model observability, formal verification of code, better agent sandboxing, new open identity and authentication standards, and cryptographic attestation of models and runtimes, and so much more.

Spiral grants are typically for 12 months with a value of $100K USD. We look for talented contributors around the globe who can work remotely. In addition to the grant, you will have complete freedom to direct your own project, be eligible for a travel stipend and gain access to a network of former Spiral grantees who have gone on to work for major companies or start their own companies.
Our grant program continues giving back long after the grant is gone.
To apply for a grant, send a detailed proposal—with a focus on the scale and longevity of impact of your project and its unique contribution—to grants@spiral.xyz. Or just smash the button.

Our mission at Stacks is to unlock hundreds of billions of dollars in capital and build a global economy on top of Bitcoin. We prioritize builders who have the same shared mission, using the Stacks' cutting edge infrastructure.

Grants are how we invest in the future of the Stacks ecosystem. By funding infrastructure, adoption, and community-led work, we help ensure Stacks grows sustainably, securely, and in ways the entire ecosystem can build on.
We believe the Stacks ecosystem grows strongest when ambitious builders are empowered to ship, measure real impact, and create long-term value rooted in Bitcoin.

Our grant program is designed to support builders at every stage, from early experimentation to proven protocols, with capital, guidance, and accountability. Whether you’re launching new infrastructure, scaling a live product, or strengthening the social fabric of the ecosystem, our goal is the same: help bold ideas take off and grow.
A clear, simple description of the product, protocol, or tool you’re creating. Focus on what it does and who it’s for.
Explain the problem you’re solving and why it’s important to the community. Show the impact, not just the idea.
Break down how the funds will be spent (development, design, marketing, tooling). Keep it practical and transparent.
Define how you’ll track progress and outcomes: milestones, users, deployments, or adoption metrics.
Include links to past projects, GitHub, onchain dashboards or community contributions. Show us you’re real, engaged, and ready to ship.

Builder grants fund teams shipping real products, infrastructure and tools on Stacks. This tracks values measurable impact and long-term creation that moves us toward a more open, equitable internet powered by Bitcoin.

This is where most builders begin: you have a novel idea and need support to bring it to life. Many developers come from our hackathons or DevRel programs to fund their first serious project. This track is for pre product market fit founders and small teams who have prototypes, technical spec, early user research, or real community traction.

This track funds the people who make Stacks feel like home: local organizers, educators, artists, content creators, and community builders who strengthen our social and cultural fabric. This program is completely run by the community with operational support from the Endowment.
We back founders and teams who can build exceptional products. Your track record, demonstrated expertise, or early proof-of-concept should show you're ready to execute.

Show us how funding translates into progress. Whether it's TVL targets, user metrics, code deliverables, or community engagement, we need to see specific milestones, realistic timelines, and honest budget breakdowns.

Your project should leverage what makes Stacks unique: Bitcoin security through Proof of Transfer, Clarity's predictability, sBTC's potential, or our layer architecture. We're looking for ideas that couldn't exist or thrive anywhere else.

The best projects make everyone stronger. Whether you're building infrastructure that others can build on, creating liquidity that protocols can tap into, or producing tools that make developers' lives easier, we prioritize applications that create composable, long-term value for the entire ecosystem.

name: StarkWare
description: StarkWare is excited to announce the launch of a $4 million venture fund to foster the growth of blockchain startups in Africa. The fund is a testament to StarkWare’s belief in the potential of blockchain in Africa, a continent historically underserved by traditional institutions, to drive global crypto adoption.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: StarkWare is excited to announce the launch of a $4 million venture fund to foster the growth of blockchain startups in Africa. The fund is a testament to StarkWare’s belief in the potential of blockchain in Africa, a continent historically underserved by traditional institutions, to drive global crypto adoption.

The Africa-focused venture fund is spearheaded by Kheireddine Kamal, a seasoned African entrepreneur and investor. Kamal brings deep experience in business development, blockchain, and seed investments to the initiative, having worked with several startups across the continent.

The Africa investment team will focus on early-stage teams, particularly those at the pre-seed and seed stages, with an emphasis on projects aiming to deploy their solutions on Starknet, the zero-knowledge (ZK) rollup massively scaling Ethereum.

sections.heading: Grants and investment opportunities
paragraphs: Early-stage startups can apply for grants of up to $150,000, with larger investments available to more advanced teams (generally up to $500,000). Grants are designed to help projects at different stages of development. StarkWare is particularly interested in teams that combine technical expertise with business acumen, and are looking to deploy their blockchain projects on Starknet.

sections.heading: A region primed for blockchain adoption
paragraphs: Africa is expected to house a third of the world’s youth by 2025. The region’s economic outlook is also promising, with $6.7 trillion in consumer and business spending forecast by 2030. When viewing those stats alongside a 2,500% surge in crypto adoption since 2021, it’s clear Africa is ripe for blockchain adoption.

Kamal’s focus for the fund is to target regions with populations that are eager to embrace blockchain, such as West Africa, East Africa, and South Africa, where many resourceful and resilient entrepreneurs face structural barriers, such as high transaction fees, broken financial systems, and exclusion from the global digital economy. By combining funding, mentorship, and technical expertise, this initiative will help African founders overcome these challenges and scale their projects globally.

sections.heading: Empowering the African tech ecosystem
paragraphs: Kamal, a Moroccan-born entrepreneur with a wealth of experience in the tech ecosystem, is passionate about empowering Africa’s digital economy. Having lived and worked across South Africa and other parts of the continent, Kamal has witnessed firsthand the transformative power of technology. He stresses that for Africa, Web3 is not just another technology, but rather a gateway to self-sovereignty and financial independence.

“For much of the blockchain industry, talk of financial inclusion for the unbanked and benefits for Africa has never gone beyond virtue signaling,” said Kamal in the announcement of the fund. “We’ve decided it’s time for the next phase, and we’re putting our money where our mouths are.”

Starknet, specifically, provides a significant catalyst for African blockchain adoption. As a Layer 2 network scaling Ethereum, Starknet offers speed (2-second transaction confirmation), cost effectiveness (sub-cent fees), and expansive network capacity, which are essential for addressing the needs of Africa’s rapidly growing digital economy.

sections.heading: A vision for Africa’s future
paragraphs: Eli Ben-Sasson, CEO and co-founder of StarkWare, emphasized blockchain’s unique opportunity for Africa:

“Blockchain presents a unique opportunity for many parts of Africa to leapfrog outdated infrastructures and democratize access to financial tools with more decentralization and transparency. And Africa is an exciting mass market that will drive innovation, and showcase what can be achieved with mass scale.”

StarkWare’s new venture fund is a step toward realizing the transformative potential of blockchain in Africa. By empowering startups and supporting the continent’s rapidly evolving digital landscape, StarkWare is helping lay the foundation for Africa’s blockchain-driven future.
If you are a founder in Africa and are interested in learning more, please contact Kheireddine Kamal directly by email or on X.

paragraphs: 💸 Get up to $10,000 in DD.xyz API credits to add an extra layer of due diligence to your dApp Integrate Webacy's robust APIs to equip you and your users with the critical intelligence needed for effective due diligence and decentralized decision-making within the web3 ecosystem. Empower them with the tools to navigate the landscape confidently and make informed choices. Webacy's Risk Engine is at the core of all out API endpoints. This powerful engine provides the broadest coverage across the blockchain ecosystem by aggregating data from over 15 diverse data providers, complemented by our proprietary data analytics and advanced algorithms. We process millions of signals monthly, incorporating the latest and most up-to-date information spanning compliance, regulatory data, potential threats, and community-sourced insights. What does this mean for your integration? By utilizing DD.xys’ APIs, you provide your users with access to the most extensive and current risk-related data available. Unlike solutions relying on a single data source, our multi-provider approach offers a comprehensive and nuanced understanding of the complexities within web3. Our engine combines the power of AI-driven analysis with human refinement, ensuring both efficient processing and highly accurate information for user evaluation. Facilitating informed decision-making requires providing relevant data across the web3 journey. Our APIs deliver crucial insights at key interaction points: Wallet Risk Insights: Enable users to understand the risk profiles associated with different wallets and their activities. Transaction Intelligence: Provide users with data to evaluate the potential risks associated with specific transactions. Token Analysis: Equip users with comprehensive data and risk assessments for all tokens Smart Contract Analysis: Offer users information to assess the security and potential risks of interacting with various smart contracts. Contextual Awareness: Equip users with the information needed to understand the broader context surrounding their web3 interactions. The DD.xyz Platform is architected to empower projects and end-users throughout their web3 experience. Our APIs are designed to be valuable at every stage, providing the data necessary for individuals to conduct their own due diligence and make well-informed decisions. Built by a team with deep expertise in crypto, cybersecurity, AI, and data integration, Webacy provides the foundational data layer for informed participation in web3. We process vast amounts of information, allowing your users to access critical intelligence and exercise greater autonomy in their web3 journey. Integrate our infrastructure and empower your users with the knowledge they need to navigate web3 with confidence. 🗳️ Apply for the grant now. We are receiving a large volume of applications, and may not have the time to give detailed feedback on every submission. Please keep that in mind before you apply. 👩🏻‍💻 Our APIs Threat Risks API This API discovers the risk of any on-chain address. This includes any contract, wallet, EOA (Externally Owned Account), token, NFT, or otherwise. It analyzes an address' threat to others. It returns risk data associated with the supplied address. It flags if the address appears in any sanctioned databases or has been historically flagged as malicious. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Filtering addresses for spam/sybil Blocking high-risk addresses from utilizing your service (compliance, platform safety) Flagging high-risk addresses (tokens, contracts, P2P participants) Example implementation: Block, limit and/or track unwanted addresses (like spam, bots, clones, OFAC/SCAM/Blacklisted/Terrorism financing addresses) from entering/signing in to your platform. Highlighting token risk analysis prior to a swap, or within a users wallet. Approval Risks API This API analyzes the risks associated with token approvals given by a specific address. It returns data indicating potentially risky approvals, such as those granting unlimited allowance to suspicious contracts. This helps users understand and manage their token permissions. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Alerting users about potentially dangerous token approvals Providing insights into a user's approval history Identifying and mitigating risks related to token drain attacks Example implementation: Display historical risk data to a user. Better understand a user’s behavioral patterns. Provide recommendations to users based on transactional health history. Assess a user’s historical activity in order to approve or adjust a loan or financial terms. Transaction Risks API This API returns risk data associated with a given transaction. It incorporates various risk factors, including the risk profiles of the involved addresses (both sender and receiver) and the risk associated with the smart contract being interacted with. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Evaluating the risk level of transactions occurring on your platform Providing users with risk assessments before they confirm transactions Implementing fraud detection mechanisms Example implementation: Exposure Risk API This API returns the 'risk profile' of a given address. It indicates the level of exposure the address has to risky activities based on its historical transactions, on-chain behavior, and the risk profiles of the assets it holds. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Understanding the overall risk level of a user's wallet Identifying users with high exposure to risky entities or activities Tailoring risk mitigation strategies based on a user's exposure profile Example implementation: Add an UI element so once the user connects their wallet, they’ll be able to see how safe it is (low/medium/safe/safest) directly in your dApp. For example, an infographic “Safety Score: LOW”. Contract Risk API This API analyzes the risk associated with a given smart contract address. It returns data points and risk scores related to the contract's security, potential vulnerabilities, and historical behavior. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Evaluating the safety of smart contracts before interacting with them Providing users with risk assessments of smart contracts Identifying potentially malicious or vulnerable contracts Identifying past behaviour of contract deployer Example Implementation: Flag tokens, NFTs, NFT collections or addresses in your platform with an UI element in the case they are malicious. Let your users know that the address might be malicious and that they should DYOR. We’ve seen the most demand coming from exchanges, swaps, bridges, DeFi protocols and launchpads. URL Risk This API analyzes the safety of a given URL. It determines if the URL is associated with phishing scams, malware distribution, or other malicious activities. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Protecting users from phishing attacks by identifying malicious URLs Scanning URLs before allowing users to navigate to them within your application Identifying and blocking known malicious websites Common use case: Quest and SocialFi platforms integrate URL Risk API to check/block/track/limit if any URL/link their users post is malicious/drainer/phishing. Holder Analysis API (Invite Only Endpoint) This API provides detailed analysis of the early holders of a specific token. It returns data points related to the distribution of the token among early adopters, identifying potential risks associated with concentrated ownership or suspicious early activity. Some common use cases for this endpoint include: Conducting due diligence on new tokens Identifying potential risks related to token distribution Providing insights into the early dynamics of a token's ownership Example implementation: AI Agents or trading bots highlighting high bundling or sniping as an issue and not interacting with a potential rug-pull. Highlighting bundling/sniping history prior to a swap.  ⚙️ How it works Submit the application form (won’t take more than 10 minutes!). Wait for 72 hours to hear back with a decision. If approved, you'll receive an email notification for onboarding and further steps.  🤝 Guidelines Be concise & precise: Being clear and concise is always helpful. Bonus points if the application contains well-defined technical details (wherever required). Don’t hesitate to contact us to amend or edit your requirements: Beyond what is specified, if you have any unique insight regarding what your current needs are, feel free to reach out to us info@webacy.com.  Do your homework: Read our API docs, research about Webacy and ask questions if needed. Differentiation: Your application should make it clear how your project is differentiated from other similar projects across relevant ecosystems. ❓Frequently asked questions Where can I read more information about Webacy and its APIs? You can access more information at  https://docs.webacy.com/   What chains do you support? We support Solana, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, BSC, Sei, Sui, Stellar, Ton, and Base. More on the roadmap How much time do I have to integrate?  You have up to 3 months to integrate but the integration agreement should be signed as soon as you are selected as grant winner. Are there any other benefits? Yes, amongst other benefits are co-marketing (access to an audience of over 250,000 unique users) and Webacy PRO access passes for your community or users. Can I whitelabel the frontend UI of the integration? Yes, you can choose whether to add DD.xyz logo/name, or make it completely yours. We can also provide you with a JavaScript snippet which you can copy and paste for the frontend UI. Who is eligible to apply for the grant? Any dApp that supports and is building on Solana, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, BSC, Sei, Ton and Base What criteria will the panelists use to evaluate grants? We prefer projects that 1) yield results quickly 2) are executable by the proposing team. What conditions apply? The only condition is that you periodically update us about the API integration stage and you actively communicate. Will I receive feedback on my proposal if it is rejected? To the best of our abilities given the large volume of submissions.  🗳️ Apply for the grant now.

name: Stellar Foundation - Academic Research Grant
description: Students and researchers can earn academic grants from SDF up to $150,000 in USD. Grants are awarded to research proposals that advance SDF's goals of financial inclusion, fast and inexpensive cross-border payments, efficient decentralized markets, and other beneficial applications of distributed ledger technology.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: The Stellar Development Foundation is soliciting proposals for scientific, technological, economic, and legal research advancing the foundation’s goals of financial inclusion, fast and inexpensive cross-border payments, efficient decentralized markets, and other beneficial applications of blockchain technology.

Awards will be provided to academic institutions as unrestricted gifts intended to support an individual with PI status. The funds are intended to support the cost of one graduate student or one post-doc for 12 months, plus reasonable expenses such as conference travel. To qualify, your institution must be a degree-granting institution whose primary mission is research or higher education, and your institution must be able to confirm that you are authorized to lead research (PI status). Students, consultants, for-profit businesses, and other institutions that do not grant degrees are not eligible. Awards are paid to academic institutions only and never to individuals. If you do not qualify, please take a look at the Stellar Community Fund instead.

sections.heading: Topics​
paragraphs: Topics of interest include but are not limited to:
Proposals should propose to make novel scientific contributions, and activities such a literature reviews are not in scope (we expect PIs to be experts in the fields of the proposal).
bullets: Privacy-preserving technology, including improvements to both efficiency and regulatory compliance of private payments
Formal verification, including verification of smart contracts and distributed systems
Research related to the Federated Byzantine Agreement model
Scalability solutions for order-books and smart-contracts, including deterministic parallel transaction execution
Legal theories and implications surrounding usage of distributed ledgers or decentralized exchanges for physical property and securities
Incentive design for improving financial responsibility, civic engagement, or other behaviors promoting financial security and democracy

sections.heading: Applying for a grant​
paragraphs: We review grant proposals quarterly. The submission deadlines are March 31, June 30, September 30, and December 31. There is a limit of maximum 2 submissions per calendar year.
Your proposal should be in PDF format, no longer than 3 pages, and in at least 11-point type, with the following outline:
To submit, please follow this link. If you have any questions, please e-mail [email protected]
bullets: One paragraph biography of principal investigator, including their current academic appointment and highlighting relevant research results and/or former students
Statement that the PI is authorized by their institution to submit research proposals and to lead research (i.e. they have PI status)
Budget not to exceed $150,000 (a rough historical average of funded proposals is $75,000)
When known, please name the student or post-doc interested in participating in the research.
Statement of intent not to patent the results, including a brief description of the principal investigator’s track record in patenting or not patenting research
If you previously received an award from SDF, add an extra page describing the work performed and the outcomes.
If this is a re-submission of a previously declined proposal, please explain briefly what changes you made.

name: Stellar Foundation - Bug Bounty Program
description: The Stellar Bug Bounty Program provides bounties for vulnerabilities and exploits discovered in the Stellar protocol or any of the code in our repos. We recognize the importance of our community and security researchers in helping identify bugs and issues. We encourage responsible disclosure of security vulnerabilities via our bug bounty program described on this page.

sections.heading: Bug bounty program
paragraphs: The Stellar Bug Bounty Program provides bounties for vulnerabilities and exploits discovered in the Stellar protocol or any of the code in our repos. We recognize the importance of our community and security researchers in helping identify bugs and issues. We encourage responsible disclosure of security vulnerabilities via our bug bounty program described on this page.

sections.heading: We're on it.
paragraphs: Our development team has up to 90 days to implement a fix based on the severity of the report. Please allow for this process to fully complete before you publicly disclose the vulnerability.

sections.heading: File a bug report
paragraphs: The Stellar Development Foundation has partnered with HackerOne, a trusted bug bounty platform, to ensure reports are handled in a fair and timely manner. Payouts vary based on the severity and impact of the report. Please refer to the HackerOne program policy for the reward scale and severity classification.
Identify vulnerabilities in the Stellar protocol and core, SDF-maintained repositories and services, and stellar.org web properties. Full scope is listed in the HackerOne program.
bullets: Try to include as much information in your report as you can, including a description of the bug, its potential -impact, and steps for reproducing it or proof of concept
Please allow 3 business days for us to respond before sending another email

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: Generally speaking, any bug that poses a significant vulnerability to the security or integrity of the Stellar network could be eligible for an award. However, it’s entirely at our discretion to decide whether a bug is significant enough to be eligible for an award.
In general, anything which has the potential for financial loss or data breach is of sufficient severity, including:
bullets: Implementation bugs that can lead to financial loss
Crash bug in Stellar Core or Horizon (ex. a bug that can crash the app by sending a special request, not by sending thousands requests)

sections.heading: Exceptions
paragraphs: In general, the following would not meet the threshold for severity:
bullets: Vulnerabilities on sites hosted by third parties unless they lead to a vulnerability on the main website
Vulnerabilities contingent on physical attack, social engineering, spamming, DDOS attack, etc
Vulnerabilities in third party applications that make use of Stellar’s API
Bugs that have not been responsibly investigated and reported
Bugs already known to us, or already reported by someone else (reward goes to first reporter)
Issues that we can’t reasonably be expected to do anything about

sections.heading: How serious is it?
paragraphs: The severity of a bug, i.e. how many participants in the Stellar network are affected, is taken into consideration when deciding the bounty payout amount. For example, an exploit that relies on an implementation bug in stellar-core affects the network as a whole and very deeply. There are no alternate implementations of stellar-core and so a payout that affects stellar-core would pay out higher than for example, an XSS bug.

description: The Matching Fund is an investment track within the Stellar Development Foundation (SDF) Enterprise Fund, designed specifically for earlier stage companies (Pre-seed to Series B) interested in building on the Stellar network. sections.heading: Stellar matching fund
paragraphs: The Matching Fund is an investment track within the Stellar Development Foundation (SDF) Enterprise Fund, designed specifically for earlier stage companies (Pre-seed to Series B) interested in building on the Stellar network. We will match investments raised from lead investors of up to $500,000 USD. This allows us more co-investment opportunities in companies with investors from around the world and helps us to grow the number of companies we can support.

Why is this important? The mission of the SDF is to provide equitable access to the global financial system. The success of our mission depends in large part on companies all over the world having access to risk capital, especially in emerging markets where investors are new to blockchain, including the Stellar network, and/or have underdeveloped venture ecosystems.

sections.heading: Investment criteria
paragraphs: All investment decisions will be made in SDF’s sole and exclusive discretion. Make sure your project meets the minimum requirements outlined below in order to be eligible for a potential Matching Fund investment.

sections.heading: 1. raise capital: secure a lead investor and submit your term sheet.
bullets: If selected, funds will be matched 1:1 up to US $500,000, with a minimum check size of US $200,000. Funding is provided in the form of USD, USDC, or XLM.
The lead investor should be an experienced investor who has made a similar type of investment within the last 12 months.
If selected, any existing SDF grants made to your company must be canceled prior to receiving a Matching Fund investment.

sections.heading: 2. the Stellar network scope: submit a description of your integration scope on the Stellar network.
bullets: Your company’s proposal must use the Stellar network in a meaningful way that aligns with the mission of SDF.
Your proposal should be a maximum of 1 page, and the proposed Stellar network integration(s) must be performed within 1 year of investment close.
Proposals from companies already building on the Stellar network must demonstrate a new or expanded use of the Stellar network. See the Enterprise Fund for areas of interest.
If selected, SDF will work with your company to finalize your integration scope.

sections.heading: 3. due diligence: submit business and legal diligence materials and participate in an SDF screening interview.
bullets: Screening interview to be conducted by at least two SDF representatives.

sections.heading: How to apply
paragraphs: To be considered for a Matching Fund investment, please complete the application form below. Please submit the following four items:
bullets: List of all investors in the round, their confirmed amounts, and how much you’re seeking from us.
Please provide a detailed explanation of your proposed integration with the Stellar network and bullet pointed list of the product scope (1 page max).
Example product scope: Within one year of investment we will create Stellar network wallets for [xx] users and enable users to send, receive, and hold Stellar network assets.

Example KPIs for estimating your impact on the Stellar network: Volume-based (GTV, send/receive volume, # of transactions), Value-based (AUM, TVL, daily or monthly transaction volume), User-based (# of wallets, DAU/MAU), and Other (key referrals or partners, etc).

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: The Story Events Grant Program is designed to expand the influence and adoption of Story within the creative and technological sectors adjacent to blockchain and AI. The Story community actively plays a crucial role in embodying the ideals laid out in the Story Manifesto, helping build a network that is open, inclusive, and actively engaged in shaping the future of Programmable IP. Season 2 Events should take place in November in support of the Surreal World Assets Buildathon. *Note: Applications for Season 2 Event Grants are now closed. The next round will open in H1 2026.* * Event Examples Programmable IP Workshops: Interactive sessions focusing on educating artists, creators, and web3 builders alike on how to use the IP Portal and ecosystem projects. Networking (Re)Mixers: Host casual get-togethers for local IP enthusiasts, creators, and tech professionals to foster community connections and discuss potential collaborations. Hackathons/Build-a-thons: Gather your local dev community! Create challenges centered around developing new applications on Story Protocol, aimed at software developers, UI/UX designers, and creatives. Gallery/studio visits: Gather the locals for a guided tour of a local art institution. Remember that these events are about building connections with the local cultural community! Dinners: Host a dinner or grab a bite with the local crypto-heads, this is a great way to make connections with other local builders interested in Programmable IP and share a bonding moment. By way of offering small grants to local community members we can simultaneously reward our community stakeholders and help the project grow. We expect you to market the event properly, and capture content that we can use to help grow Story. Please take pictures and videos. We need proof that the event happened! *Please note that nobody from the Story team will be present for the event* Funding Outline: -Community Members: For first-time or small-scale Story Community events (capped at $300), the bar is not perfection or mass adoption-it’s proof of basic competence, real engagement, and alignment with Story’s mission. The goal is to validate the organizer’s ability to deliver a focused, well-documented event that builds local momentum for programmable IP and the Story ecosystem. If these standards are hit and documented, organizers can unlock up to $2,000 for future, larger events. Please see our Post-Event Report form for an idea of how we're evaluating ROI + event metrics. -Ecosystem Projects: Up to $2000 for event support. This should serve to promote the growth of your project via event marketing. Terms and Conditions: Fill out this form to the best of your ability. If approved, we will create a telegram group to ensure you have the support you need, and open up a line of direct communications for questions and updates in regards to the event. The group invitation will come from @ngeor on telegram. Please confirm the message comes from this handle. There are scammers that impersonate Story team members daily. If denied, we'll respond via email or telegram with reasoning. You may be welcomed and encouraged to update and resubmit. Upload all content captured via the event into a Google Drive folder and share the link in the telegram channel. Adhere to the Story Community Event Hosting Guidelines. Not following these guidelines will impact the likelihood of getting approved for future grants. Note that you will need to onboard to our payments system and submit an invoice for the requested funds. The process can take up to two weeks. Please plan accordingly. Fill out the Post-Event Report within 72 hours of the event. We'll be in touch with you as soon as we can!

name: Tezos Foundations Grant Program
description: The Tezos Foundation is a non-profit organization that supports the Tezos ecosystem. The Foundation is committed to supporting the Tezos ecosystem by providing grants to projects that are aligned with the Foundation’s mission.

sections.heading: Areas of interest
paragraphs: More information about the priorities of the Tezos Foundation can be found on the Tezos Foundation website.

sections.heading: Baking
paragraphs: Tezos has a growing number of bakers in its ecosystem that help secure the network by signing and publishing blocks. Our goal is to empower bakers by supporting the development of standardized tools, tutorials and cloud applications.

sections.heading: Developer Experience
paragraphs: Our goal is to make Tezos easy to build on and onboard new developers to the ecosystem. We are looking to support tools, tutorials and documentation to improve user experience for all Tezos developers.

sections.heading: Education and Training
paragraphs: The growth and success of Tezos is heavily linked to the Tezos community. To grow and support the community, we want to enable all ecosystem members around the world.

sections.heading: End-User Applications
paragraphs: Tezos enables new types of applications, which can address problems that have been traditionally difficult to solve using legacy software stacks. We are looking to support new applications that drive wide adoption and benefit standardization, censorship-resistance, or user control on the Tezos protocol.

sections.heading: Other
paragraphs: Projects targeting categories not listed here that may advance the Tezos ecosystem!

sections.heading: Privacy
paragraphs: Censorship-resistance is key for all developments on Tezos. Our goal is to support research and development of infrastructure to build on Tezos’ strengths and enhance privacy-preserving solutions.

sections.heading: Security
paragraphs: Tezos has the assurance required for high value use cases and a focus on formal methods. Given this strength we aim to support projects building security solutions for Tezos.

sections.heading: Core Development
paragraphs: The Core Engineering and Infrastructure vertical support in the design, development and maintenance of the key software components that form the basis of the Tezos ecosystem, including the Tezos protocol, Octez and Smart Rollups. This is a collective effort of ecosystem teams – Nomadic Labs, Trilitech and Functori – where each team contributes their unique expertise to the development of the protocol and related infrastructure.
