paragraphs: The Tech.Rel Team focuses on supporting and engaging Tezos' key technical users, including developers, bakers, builders, and operators. The team ensures these users have a productive experience by providing comprehensive support, resources, and guidance. It actively captures feedback to improve product usability and incorporate this feedback into the roadmap. The team's mission is to empower technical users and enhance their interaction with Tezos products, ensuring both satisfaction and success.

Criteria: Projects should have clear objectives and goals, align with blockchain trends, demonstrate technical feasibility, and ensure sustainability and scalability. The proposals should address the needs of Tezos technical users, including bakers, builders, and integrators, in improving the usability, reliability, and adoption of the network.

sections.heading: Infrastructure & Tooling
paragraphs: The Infrastructure & Tooling Vertical for Tezos ensures the stability and performance of the Tezos blockchain by maintaining nodes, developing block explorers, and supporting smart contract languages like Michelson, Ligo and SmartPy. They handle core infrastructure development, including consensus algorithms and network protocols, and continuously optimize performance. The team creates and maintains essential tools like SDKs and APIs for developers to build, deploy, and manage dApps. Security is a top priority, with regular audits and rapid vulnerability resolution. Integration support enhances interoperability with other blockchains and technologies. Comprehensive documentation and resources are provided to help developers effectively utilize the Tezos infrastructure and tools.
Criteria: Projects should have a robust technical plan, demonstrate scalability and interoperability, ensure security and reliability, and provide comprehensive documentation and support.

sections.heading: Arts & Culture
paragraphs: Tezos has a rich history of art innovation through web3 native platforms like hic et nunc, objkt and fxhash. This dovetails with Tezos usage by globally famous institutions such as Musee d’Orsay and the Serpentine and a large number of entertainment projects including the likes of Manchester United and McLaren. The Arts and Culture vertical aims to find new and exciting ways for fans to get closer to the things they love most. Whether that is through art, sport, entertainment or other fandoms, the team is focused on supporting projects that fuel creativity and give users the chance to have a regular, deeper, more connected relationship with their passions.

Criteria: Projects should have a clear vision for regular, ongoing community engagement, promote creativity, diversity and inclusivity, foster education and understanding of Tezos. It is also crucial that all projects are backed with a strong lead/team with a clear path to onboarding users to their concept.

sections.heading: Decentralized Finance (DeFi)
paragraphs: The DeFi Vertical is dedicated to fostering a robust, thriving DeFi ecosystem within Tezos and its associated rollups. Our team is committed to promoting the growth and adoption of the Tezos blockchain in the decentralized finance domain. We collaborate closely with ecosystem teams, projects, and partners to enhance the success and impact of DeFi within Tezos and the broader Web3 community. Cryptocurrencies and the wider blockchain space at their core revolve around the idea of facilitating transfers of value online. This has led to the DeFi developments we’ve seen and continue to see and the DeFi grants program is all about facilitating the emergence of further quality DeFi and OpenFi apps on Etherlink and Tezos.

Criteria: Projects should have a secure and transparent technical framework, innovative financial solutions and robust risk management strategies. To ensure the security and reliability of DeFi projects built on our blockchain, all projects must undergo a comprehensive security audit conducted by a reputable and recognized third-party auditing firm, covering all smart contracts and relevant codebases.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Introducing [The Bags Hackathon](https://x.com/BagsHackathon) with **$4,000,000 in funding** for developers building on [Bags.fm](https://bags.fm/launch). Build good tech, win cash, start companies. We're distributing $1M in grants to 100 teams that ship real products with real traction. The remaining $3M will go into [The Bags Fund](https://x.com/BagsFund) to support builders with capital, distribution, and more.
100 winners are selected based on real traction: onchain performance, app usage, and growth potential. Early traction and growth trajectory weigh heavily in our evaluation.
Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Apply now to be accepted into the first cohort.

sections.heading: Rules
paragraphs: The top 100 projects each receive a grant between $10,000 and $100,000. Winners can apply to the Bags Fund for ongoing support with listings, capital, and more. Projects that ship and get traction will be rewarded.

Winners are ranked holistically across two dimensions: onchain performance (market cap, volume, active traders, etc.) and app traction (MRR, DAU, Github Stars, etc.). New projects are also eligible and early signs of growth weigh heavily in our evaluation.
All winning projects must be verified onchain. We verify the team, the contract, and the revenue. Ownership is confirmed and everything is publicly verifiable.
Your project must have a Bags token, use the Bags API, or release a fee sharing app. Deeper integrations rank higher.

Ideas alone don't qualify. You must deploy a working product with real users and real transaction. Prototypes are accepted at application, but grants are distributed to shipped products. We reserve the right to evaluate projects qualitatively.
There is no single deadline. Applications are open throughout Q1, reviewed continuously, and grants are distributed as projects are accepted and verified.

sections.heading: How winners are ranked
paragraphs: Projects are evaluated across two dimensions. For new projects, early signs of growth weigh heavily.
Market Cap, Volume, Active Traders, Revenue, + more.

sections.heading: Bonus prizes

sections.heading: About applying

name: Thiel Fellowship
description: A two-year, $100,000 grant given to 20-25 young founders and researchers under 22 who want to build new things instead of sitting in a classroom.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: The Thiel Fellowship gives $250,000 to young people who want to build new things instead of sitting in a classroom.

sections.heading: What
paragraphs: Founded by technology entrepreneur and investor Peter Thiel in 2011, the Thiel Fellowship is a two-year program for young people who want to build new things. Thiel Fellows skip or stop out of college to receive a $250,000 grant and support from the Thiel Foundation’s network of founders, investors, and scientists.

sections.heading: Why
paragraphs: “Knowledge that is acquired under compulsion obtains no hold on the mind.”

College can be good for learning about what’s been done before, but it can also discourage you from doing something new. Each of our fellows charts a unique course; together they have proven that young people can succeed by thinking for themselves instead of following a traditional track and competing on old career tracks.
“My grandmother wanted me to have an education, so she kept me out of school”

Pursue ideas that matter instead of mandatory tests. Take on big risks instead of big debt. How you spend your two years in the Fellowship is up to you — we’re here to help, but we won’t get in the way.
“That major that she majored in don't make no money / But she won't drop out, her parents'll look at her funny”

The hardest thing about being a young entrepreneur is that you haven’t met everyone you’ll need to know to make your venture succeed. We can help connect you — to investors, partners, prospective customers — in Silicon Valley and beyond.

sections.heading: As seen in
paragraphs: “Thanks to the Thiel Fellowship, access to some of the nation’s most successful businesspeople is quick and easy.”

“Thiel’s fellowship pays kids a stipend that liberates them to work on ways to improve the world, rather than saddling them with debt. They get mentorship, workshops, connections to resources, and an alumni network without a formal alma mater.”
“Not long ago, dropping out of school to start a company was considered risky. For this generation, it is a badge of honor, evidence of ambition and focus.”

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: Audiences Post, Communities Host TL;DR: All our feeds are cooked and touching grass with friends is the final defense. The Superteam touching grass fund is here to support members who host, not just post. Get up to $500 USDG to cover expenses for organizing Solana & Superteam adjacent meet-ups in your city, as per the guidelines below. Social media platforms are no longer social. By default, you don't see content from your friends, family, or people you're connected with. Instead, our feeds are dominated by sophisticated professionals who are engineering content to elicit a dopamine response while competing for max share of our attention that they can then package and sell to sponsors. In such times, IRL events are the last defense to compete with brainrot. Audiences post, communities host : A big focus for each Superteam is to be the frontier onboarding vehicle for the most promising talent in their local markets. However, the magic happens when members go from sharing memes in a group chat to forming teams on Solana, and often forge lifelong friendships in the process. The optimal way to participate in Superteam is to use the access & trust from being a member to find your niche interest and the people you can collaborate with to create weekend projects, products, or companies around it. Those who do it right will find themselves in more group chats than they can count, spontaneously joining Zoom calls and taking cabs/trains/planes to meet their internet friends. More on this idea in a previous blog post here . Therefore, Superteam now supports the Solana Foundation community grants program and recommends applicants with the ability to galvanize the community with in-person events for community grants. Members are encouraged to host casual events like coffee mixers, dinners, paddle or pickleball tournaments, turf football or cricket, or more structured events like learning groups, weekend hackathons, bounty hunting, or co-working sessions. As long as you're doing something that (a) brings the Solana community closer together and (b) onboards those on the sidelines into crypto, feel free to apply. Currently, only Superteam members can be hosts, but anyone can attend. If this format works, we will drop the host restriction and open it up to anyone in the Superteam ecosystem. 🤝 Events Playbook The meetups are supposed to be a lot of fun, but it's not all there is to a valuable meetup. To have a higher chance of success—and to get more from the touching grass fund down the line—we recommend doing as many of these as possible: Limited attendees: Invite a small group of not more than 8–10 people. Focus on a size and venue that enables everyone to talk to everyone else at least once. A generic meetup isn't the best fit for this; we're only looking to support meetups where attendees are: developers, operators (marketing, product, ops), creators (writers, researchers, YouTubers, etc.), investors (both angels and VCs), founders, and capital markets professionals. Primer on crypto: Depending on how much is necessary, help folks find their way into the Superteam and Solana ecosystem. Make them feel at home! Merch (optional): Coordinate with your local Superteam team to get merch—T-shirts, stickers, bags, etc.—for attendees to take back as a souvenir. Food & Coffee: If this is part of your event, an ideal meal is one where (1) everyone can talk to each other, and (2) it's reasonably priced and prudently ordered without wasting food or money. Onboarding: If you're inviting people who are new to crypto or Solana, ideally you should also act as their buddy & help them find their pathway to contribution via bounties, gigs, jobs, hackathons, asset onboarding/distribution, etc. Proof of meet-up: Ideally, take pictures and put them up on your social media of choice with a short caption sharing your experience, learnings, or thoughts. Tag your local Superteam as they might share it as well! Follow-up group: Invite everyone who attends into a private Telegram/WhatsApp group that you're an admin of. This way you can stay in touch and help make more plans that were discussed at dinner! What this grant is not for: Events that are purely social or personal with no direct link to Solana or Superteam goals. Misuse of funds or falsified reports can potentially result in being purged from the Superteam membership. ⚙️ How It Works Create a private event page on Luma. Please ensure you've added an appropriate title, cover image, and a full description of the event — including the format of the event, schedule if any, who the event is for, outcomes for the event, etc. Make a grant application for it here on Earn, and include the private Luma link of your event in the application. Sponsors will usually reply within ~7 days. If approved, you'll receive a confirmation email. Once approved: Submit your event to the  Superteam Calendar  so it's visible to the broader community. You'll receive 50% of the grant upfront (post KYC; to be done on this page on Earn) in the following weekly payout cycle. Approved KYC and payments are sent for processing on Mondays and paid to you by Friday of the same week. After the event, upload photos from the event + scanned copies of expense receipts from the event to the tranche application form on this listing. This tranche application form will be visible to you after you have received your first tranche. Both the photos from the event and scanned copies of the receipts are essential for processing your second tranche. ❓ Frequently Asked Questions Who is eligible to apply for event grants? This program is currently in beta and only open for Superteam Members. What criteria will the panelists use to evaluate grants? We prefer to support members that have some prior experience in organizing events (regardless of how small) and events that are primarily focused on developers, artists, and investors. Will I receive feedback on my proposal if it is rejected? Unfortunately, our sponsors do not have the bandwidth to provide individualized feedback at this time.   Note: Getting approved for a grant is in no way to be understood as an endorsement or partnership. Your event will be a community event, and in no way should you represent to third parties that it's a "Superteam event" or in any sense official.   🚁 Have a question that isn't answered here?  Email us at support@superteam.fun  for help.

The Venom Blockchain has plenty of unique features that differentiate it from other blockchains.

Venom Blockchain is built on the Threaded Virtual Machine (TVM). TVM provides a highly efficient and scalable way to handle account interactions in the Venom Blockchain. By utilizing the Actor model, TVM can isolate and parallelize actors, allowing for the efficient handling of complex distributed systems. This makes the dynamic sharding protocol further groups account into shards, improving efficiency and enabling contracts to execute in an asynchronous mode.

Venom Blockchain is built on the Threaded Virtual Machine (TVM). TVM provides a highly efficient and scalable way to handle account interactions in the Venom Blockchain. By utilizing the Actor model, TVM can isolate and parallelize actors, allowing for the efficient handling of complex distributed systems. This makes the dynamic sharding protocol further groups account into shards, improving efficiency and enabling contracts to execute in an asynchronous mode.

Blockchain account abstraction is typically achieved through smart contracts, which are self-executing contracts with the terms of the agreement written directly into code. Smart contracts define the account's behavior and specify the rules for interacting with it, such as how to check the balance or transfer assets.
The Venom Blockchain provides developers greater flexibility and modularity in their dApp designs by abstracting the functionality of an account into a smart contract.

External messaging is a crucial feature in Venom that allows the blockchain to interact with the external world seamlessly. By bridging the gap between off-chain and on-chain systems, the Venom blockchain is able to receive data and events from external sources and use that information to trigger actions inside the blockchain network, even if the sender doesn't have an on-chain entity.
This powerful capability can support the off-chain data-providing network in the Venom Blockchain.

Workchains in the Venom blockchain offer a flexible and efficient way of meeting the diverse needs of different applications across industries. With different levels of security, compliance, and privacy requirements, workchains provide specialized layer-1 blockchains that can cater to specific needs. Public, private, and consortium workchains offer a range of options for users to choose from and customize based on their specific requirements.

T-Sol is the developer-friendly language offering unlimitless potential and ease of use. Due to the fact that T-Sol is derived from Solidity, developers with existing experience in C, C++, Javascript, and C# can enduldge in a frictionless onboarding due to syntax similarity.
T-Sol provides developers the tools to create complex smart contracts that interact with other Venom blockchain accounts.

Locklift is a development framework aiming to help users with Venom contract development. It is designed to be modular and flexible, allowing developers to choose the tools and libraries that best fit their specific project needs. It includes a wide range of features, including network management, automated testing, a convenient abstraction for Venom contracts, support for custom accounts, key management, and an external script runner to execute scripts in a specific environment.

The Venom Knowledge Base is a comprehensive resource for developers and enthusiasts who want to learn about the Venom blockchain. It is an entry point into the Venom universe that provides clear and concise information about the various aspects of the blockchain, including its architecture, consensus mechanism, virtual machine, and more.
Whether you are new to blockchain technology or an experienced developer, the Venom Knowledge Base offers valuable insights how the blockchain works and how to use it effectively.
Venom is a versatile and innovative blockchain that offers a range of use cases across various industries.

DAOs (Decentralized Autonomous Organizations) are organizations that run on a blockchain network, where decisions are made through a voting system that's open to anyone who holds the organization's tokens. This means that members have a direct say in how the organization operates, without needing a central authority to make decisions for them.Some use cases for DAOs include managing community projects, creating decentralized investment funds, and even running online social networks.

Projects are expected to contribute to the following outcomes:

In the recent years, hardware for Virtual Worlds made major breakthroughs, democratising headsets, sensors, actuators or haptic equipment. To keep this momentum and advancing further, new generation of XR equipment, wearable solutions and haptic components, as well as non-invasive brain computer interfaces for handsfree interaction, hardware or technologies will put the users at the very centre of virtual experiences, for even greater and realistic immersion, aiming at blurring the lines between the real and digital environments. To ensure this next generation of engaging and lifelike immersion, all senses must be stimulated (sight, hearing, feel, touch, smell), for a fully immersive close-to-reality experience. Users will be submerged with realistic sensations making the experience as immersive as possible.
Proposals should investigate novel scientific approaches or push the limit of existing ones to improve the synchronization and integration of the different modalities.

Proposals are expected to integrate various components in fully tested devices, demonstrating the usefulness and efficiency of their system in illustrative scenarios in the industrial and societal contexts.
Proposals should focus on performant, reliable, miniaturised, interoperable advanced and innovative technologies, with inclusivity, energy consumption and energy efficiency at the centre of concerns.

This topic requires the effective contribution of SSH disciplines and the involvement of SSH experts, institutions as well as the inclusion of relevant SSH expertise, in order to produce meaningful and significant effects enhancing the societal impact of the related research activities.

The Consortium should pay attention to developing solutions that are reliable, robust and interoperable. Proposals should leverage existing open standards and technologies in the domain of Virtual Worlds, while contributing to ongoing standardisation work.

sections.heading: About the Program
paragraphs: X1 EcoChain is an energy-efficient L1 (PoN) with ~3W nodes and ultra-low fees. The $5M program accelerates dApps and tooling that drive on-chain activity and users to X1. Priority: 90–120 days to deploy (testnet/mainnet), strong security and code quality, clear GTM and adoption metrics.
bullets: X1 EcoChain’s mission is to deliver best-in-class, energy-efficient Web4 infrastructure for teams of any size — from early startups to established enterprises — via an EVM, Proof-of-Nodes L1 with ~3Wh home nodes and sub-cent fees.

This grant program is reserved for innovators building and launching high-utility products on X1 EcoChain — spanning DePIN, Infrastructure/Tooling, Finance & Commerce, Consumer/Social, and Gaming — with clear user value and measurable on-chain activity.

The $5M X1 Ecosystem Program empowers builders to push what’s possible onchain and bring practical, secure, and scalable innovations to users worldwide, with milestone-based support across grants, infra credits, liquidity & GTM.

X1 Ecosystem Grants include several tracks tailored to each team’s needs. Applications are evaluated on impact, readiness (90–120 day deployment plan), security, ecosystem fit, and compliance; awards are sized accordingly for eligible projects.

paragraphs: All teams building on X1 EcoChain (EVM, PoN) or integrating X1 into their products are eligible to apply for X1 Ecosystem Grants. There are four categories of Web4 innovators eligible for X1 EcoChain grants:
Projects piloting home/edge nodes (validators, sensors, mobile/IoT) that create verifiable on-chain activity and demonstrate energy-efficient operation on X1 EcoChain.
Teams in stealth or pre-launch preparing for product/platform releases, testnet/mainnet deployments, TGEs, betas, or airdrop programs, with a 90–120 day delivery plan.
AI-integrated apps or core infra (compute / storage / indexing / oracles / wallets / dev tools) with enterprise-grade reliability, clear security practices, and measurable developer adoption.
User-facing products with growing engagement and high volumes of on-chain transactions (e.g., social graphs, payments, gaming), aiming to scale active users on X1 EcoChain.

name: XRPL Commons Grants Program
description: The XRP Ledger ecosystem is entering a new phase. The XRPL Commons Grants Program operates across three tracks, each targeting a distinct builder profile.

sections.heading: Conversation
bullets: LOBSTR Wallet@lobstrJul 23Proud to be one of the pillars8347

sections.heading: Introducing the XRPL Commons Grants Program
paragraphs: XRP Ledger's next phase of growth is being built by many, funded by many. Here's our part.

The XRP Ledger ecosystem is entering a new phase. Over $550 million has been invested in the XRP Ledger ecosystem since 2017, and the model is shifting: toward a distributed network of independent organizations, each supporting builders in their own way. XRPL Commons is one of those pillars.

Since 2023, we've run The Aquarium, an incubator for MVP-stage projects on the XRP Ledger, trained hundreds of developers, and launched the Glow retroactive funding program for open-source contributors. Today, we're formalizing the full structure of how we support builders across three tracks, for builders at every stage.

sections.heading: How the program is structured
paragraphs: The XRPL Commons Grants Program operates across three tracks, each targeting a distinct builder profile.

Glow is our retroactive funding and bounty program for open-source contributors to the XRP Ledger. If you've built open-source tooling the ecosystem depends on, documented something that saved developers time, or significantly contributed to protocol infrastructure, Glow is for you.

The program launched in October 2025 and has since funded 11 projects, including node management tooling, transactional dashboards, post-quantum integrations, and more. We've published a 5-months in retrospective of what worked and what didn't.
Glow now runs on a quarterly cadence: open applications, no referral required. The program is 60% disbursed and runs through December 2026. → Apply to Glow
2. Building on the XRPL: Incubate, Ship, Scale
This track supports early-stage projects building on the XRP Ledger, from first idea to live product. It spans three mechanisms that work together.

Make Waves is a 90-day live challenge that kicked off on June 21st, 2026. Builders have until September 21st to ship and grow an app on the XRPL mainnet. The program rewards the projects with the most users and highest on-chain volume, with a 25,000 XRP grand prize and additional prizes for top performers. A bonus is available for the first 15 apps to reach 300 users.

The Aquarium is a 9-week incubation program launched in 2023. Initially run out of Paris, the program is transitioning to online for wider accessibility. It supports developers and founders building within the XRP Ledger ecosystem, providing hands-on mentorship, technical guidance, and direct access to the XRPL Commons team and network. For a selection of projects, this is followed by a 90-day online sprint to unlock growth. Aquarium alumni get priority access to our Early Stage Grants. → Apply to The Aquarium

Early Stage Grants provide individual small grants for projects building on XRP Ledger rails. Grants are milestone-based and cover both technical integration and growth targets. Every grantee gets hands-on support from the XRPL Commons team on architecture, technical integration, and go-to-market strategy.

What we look for: a working product live on testnet or mainnet, a clear path to generating volume on XRPL, and a team that knows what they're building. We don't fund ideas. → We'll open applications in September.
We're currently focused on EMEA, with priority access for hackathon winners and Aquarium alums.

The third track works with established products — proven teams with existing user bases on other chains — to integrate XRP Ledger infrastructure where it fits. This comes with hands-on support from the XRPL Commons team on technical integration and go-to-market planning.
One recent example: LOBSTR, a powerful wallet on Stellar, has integrated XRPL support in partnership with XRPL Commons, enabling its users to access the XRP Ledger directly.

We're actively identifying further partners in DeFi, agentic finance and payments. If you lead an established project and want to explore what XRPL rails could mean for your product, reach out directly.

XRPL's protocol-level capabilities are what make these integrations interesting: a native DEX with no MEV and no front-running, a Permissioned DEX for regulated and credentialed trading, compliance infrastructure built into the protocol rather than layered on top, and advanced payment primitives including escrow, cross-currency settlement, and payment channels. For products operating in regulated environments, or building around stablecoins and tokenized real-world assets, this reduces engineering and legal overhead that other chains require you to build yourself.

The XRP Ledger has processed over 3.7 billion transactions since its genesis, with average daily transactions up 35.3% quarter-over-quarter to 2.48 million as network usage accelerates (Messari Q1 2026 report). Real-world asset value on XRPL has grown even faster — jumping 124.1% quarter-over-quarter to a record $2.25 billion — while the ledger settles transactions in 3-5 seconds for a fraction of a cent. With regulatory clarity now established across the US, UK, EU, and other major markets, the XRP Ledger continues to build the infrastructure for global, real-world financial applications.

sections.heading: A full-stack approach to ecosystem development
paragraphs: Funding is one part of how ecosystems grow. The other part is support to help a developer understand the protocol, a founder to ship their product, and a team to navigate a new chain's technical and market landscape.

XRPL Commons combines both. The grants program sits inside a broader infrastructure: training programs, The Aquarium incubator, builder challenges, a developer community, and a team that works alongside grantees through technical integration and go-to-market.

sections.heading: At a glance
paragraphs: Glow: for Open-source contributors - Live — apply now
The Aquarium: For early stage founders and developers with an MVP: Applications open
Make Waves: For app builders : Live — closes Sept 21
Early Stage Grants: For MVP-stage projects: applications open in September
Strategic integrations: For established projects who want to add XRP Ledger rails : by invitation / direct outreach
XRPL Commons is a non-profit organization dedicated to growing the XRP Ledger ecosystem through education, community, and ecosystem development.

description: The Zcash Community Grants program funds independent teams entering the Zcash ecosystem, to perform major ongoing development (or other work) for the public good of the Zcash ecosystem.

sections.heading: Program overview
paragraphs: The Zcash Community Grants program (formerly known as ZOMG) funds independent teams entering the Zcash ecosystem, to perform major ongoing development (or other work) for the public good of the Zcash ecosystem.
Funding for Zcash Community Grants comes from the Major Grants slice of the Zcash Dev Fund. Grants are chosen by a five-person committee elected by the Zcash Community.

[ZIP-1014](https://zips.z.cash/zip-1014), [ZIP-1015](https://zips.z.cash/zip-1015)&[ZIP-1016](https://zips.z.cash/zip-1016) were approved by the Zcash community, allocating 8% of mining rewards to provide sustained major grant funding for the ecosystem through the third halving in November 2028.

This wishlist is meant to encourage ideas for potential applicants to improve the Zcash ecosystem and is not exhaustive. If your idea to improve Zcash doesn’t fit exactly, feel free to surprise us with your proposal!
These are some of the projects we've funded so far:
A performant, full-featured light wallet for mobile and desktop
Growing Zcash’s open-source education hub and onboarding new contributors to Zcash
A web3 platform powered by Zcash that empowers content creators
The first implementation of shielded Zcash on a hardware wallet
Bridging assets between Zcash and Avalanche using permissionless Subnet architecture
Bringing DeFi to ZEC with Zcash Shielded Assets (ZSAs)
A premiere educational platform about Zcash, privacy, and related issues.
Check [this dashboard](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1FQ28rDCyRW0TiNxrm3rgD8ai2KGUsXAjPieQmI1kKKg/edit?usp=sharing) for a complete list of grants and milestones paid.

sections.heading: What’s included in Zoom Workplace?
paragraphs: A toolkit built for teamwork — all in one affordable bundle.

sections.heading: Award-winning video conferencing
bullets: Look and sound your best with high-quality video and audio, appearance touch-ups, noise cancellation, and virtual backgrounds.
Keep everyone aligned with meeting summaries and next steps.
Collaborate effortlessly in Docs, Whiteboards, and your preferred third-party apps directly in every meeting.

sections.heading: Instant messaging, included
paragraphs: Connect your whole team — at no additional cost.
bullets: Create a chat channel for every meeting automatically, so you can message before, during, and after calls — all in one place.
Stop the scroll — get instant AI summaries of chat threads, including action items just for you.
Connect third-party apps like calendars, file storage, and CRM platforms so your workflows stay in sync and in one view.

sections.heading: Modern business phone system
paragraphs: Stay connected through an easy-to-use phone system with built-in AI — ready to scale as you grow.
bullets: Run your business from any device with a business phone number, keeping your work and personal life separate.
Let AI capture call notes and next steps, prioritize voicemails, and detect action items.
Control when and how you take calls with business hours, call routing, and more.

sections.heading: Instant scheduling
paragraphs: Say goodbye to back-and-forth emails trying to nail down a time.
bullets: Share blocks of availability through a single link.
Offer many appointment types, from one-to-one to group sessions.

bullets: Online whiteboards you can save, share, and access later.
